nodes.title: Release build, distribution, and LLM agent integration
nodes.description: Set up cross-platform release builds (GoReleaser), CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions), distribution channels (Homebrew tap), Claude Code plugin for /plugin discovery, and LLM agent kit with MCP configs and skill files. Includes supply chain security (cosign signing, reproducible builds, pinned dependencies) and release documentation (VDD, build environment baseline, metrics).
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: GoReleaser and CI/CD pipeline
nodes.description: Set up automated cross-platform builds and continuous integration. GoReleaser produces 6 platform binaries (darwin/linux/windows x amd64/arm64) with cosign signing. GitHub Actions runs tests, lint, and coverage on every push, and publishes releases on tag push.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Create .goreleaser.yaml with cosign signing
nodes.description: GoReleaser config for cross-platform binary releases with Sigstore cosign signing for supply chain integrity.
nodes.prompt: Create .goreleaser.yaml at repo root. Build ./cmd/mtix/ with CGO_ENABLED=0 and -trimpath. Targets: darwin/linux/windows x amd64/arm64. Use CommitDate (not Date) for reproducible builds in ldflags: -X main.version={{.Version}} -X main.commit={{.ShortCommit}} -X main.date={{.CommitDate}}. Archives: tar.gz for darwin/linux, zip for windows, include LICENSE, NOTICE, README.md. Checksums: sha256 in checksums.txt. Add signs: section with cosign sign-blob (keyless OIDC). Add extra_files for mtix-agent-kit tarball. Verify with: goreleaser release --snapshot --clean.
nodes.acceptance: 1. goreleaser release --snapshot --clean produces 6 binaries. 2. Each binary shows correct version via ./mtix version. 3. Checksums.txt is generated. 4. Two consecutive builds produce identical binary checksums (reproducible). 5. cosign signs section is present in config.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Create CI workflow
nodes.description: GitHub Actions CI pipeline running tests, lint, and build on every push and PR.
nodes.prompt: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml. Triggers: push to main, pull_request to main. All actions pinned to commit SHAs (not tags). Add permissions: contents: read at workflow level. Jobs: (1) test-go: matrix ubuntu-22.04 + macos-latest, setup-go 1.25, go mod verify, go test ./... -race -count=1. (2) test-web: setup-node 22, cd web && npm ci && npx vitest run. (3) lint: golangci-lint-action pinned to SHA. (4) build: depends on test-go, test-web, lint; builds web (npm ci && npm run build), copies dist to internal/web/dist/, runs go build -trimpath ./cmd/mtix/, verifies ./mtix version output. Lock all runners to ubuntu-22.04 (not ubuntu-latest).
nodes.acceptance: 1. CI runs on push to main. 2. CI runs on PRs. 3. All actions pinned to SHA with tag comment. 4. permissions: contents: read is set. 5. Tests, lint, and build all execute. 6. Runner images are pinned versions.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Create release workflow
nodes.description: GitHub Actions release pipeline triggered by version tags, with quality gates and manual approval.
nodes.prompt: Create .github/workflows/release.yml. Trigger: push tag v*.*.*. Permissions: contents: write, id-token: write (for cosign OIDC). Jobs: (1) preflight: go test -race, go test -coverprofile, npm ci && npx vitest run, golangci-lint, go mod verify. Tag-based coverage gate: if tag contains -beta or -rc, min 85%; else min 90%. Fail if git working tree is dirty. (2) release: environment: production (manual approval gate). Build web UI. SHA256 the web dist/ directory. npm audit --audit-level=high as hard gate. Generate BUILD-ENVIRONMENT.json (Go version, Node version, GoReleaser version, runner OS, commit hash). Run scripts/build-agent-kit.sh. Independent reference build: go build with same ldflags, compare checksum to GoReleaser output (BEFORE signing). Run goreleaser release --clean. Export mtix tasks.json and test results as release artifacts. Run scripts/generate-vdd.sh. (3) update-homebrew: repository-dispatch to hyper-swe/homebrew-tap. All actions pinned to commit SHAs.
nodes.acceptance: 1. Workflow triggers on v*.*.* tags only. 2. Manual approval gate via environment: production. 3. Coverage gate is tag-aware (85% beta, 90% GA). 4. Dirty tree check fails the build. 5. Web dist SHA256 is computed. 6. npm audit is a hard gate. 7. Dual-build comparison runs before signing. 8. BUILD-ENVIRONMENT.json is generated. 9. VDD is generated. 10. Tasks.json exported as artifact.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Agent ticket-creation hardening: capture-originating-context rule + CLI guardrail
nodes.description: Public-facing agent docs (AGENTS.md / SKILL.md / planning skill / PATTERNS.md) tell agents to populate description, prompt, acceptance — but never explain that 'prompt' means the originating user conversation. LLM agents are observed creating tickets with a one-line --description and empty --prompt/--acceptance/--labels, breaking the context chain for downstream agents. Two-part fix: (1) strengthen agent-facing templates with an explicit Capture-Originating-Context rule, and (2) tighten the mtix create CLI warning to fire when --prompt or --acceptance are missing (not only when all three are empty).
nodes.prompt: Decompose into two children: docs hardening and CLI guardrail. Docs work edits internal/docs/templates/{agents,skill,patterns}.md.tmpl and internal/docs/templates/skills/planning.md.tmpl, plus regenerated docs/AGENTS.md, docs/SKILL.md, docs/PATTERNS.md. CLI work edits cmd/mtix/create.go runCreate() to widen the existing all-three-empty warning to fire on missing --prompt OR --acceptance. Generic phrasing only — no skill names, repo names, or terminology from any user-shared transcript.
nodes.acceptance: Templates explicitly state the --prompt field must contain the originating user ask, file paths/symbols already discussed, constraints surfaced in the conversation, and a pointer to project skills referenced in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. PATTERNS.md has a 'lazy ticket creation' anti-pattern with fabricated example. mtix create warns on stderr when --prompt or --acceptance is empty, with message referencing the completeness test. Tests cover the new warning paths. golangci-lint clean. Coverage does not regress.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Capture-Originating-Context rule in agent-facing templates
nodes.description: Add a non-negotiable 'Capture the Originating Context' section to agents.md.tmpl, skill.md.tmpl, and skills/planning.md.tmpl. Add a 'Lazy Ticket Creation' anti-pattern to patterns.md.tmpl. Regenerate docs/AGENTS.md, docs/SKILL.md, docs/PATTERNS.md. Generic phrasing only — no user-shared skill names.

Insert a section titled 'Capture the Originating Context' under each existing 'No Code Without a Task' section. Body must state: --prompt MUST include (a) the user's verbatim ask or paraphrased intent, (b) file paths and function/symbol names already surfaced in the conversation, (c) constraints, edge cases, and decisions made before the ticket was filed, (d) a pointer to any project skills listed in the project's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md that the executing agent should invoke. Add the rule that decomposing/creating a ticket with only --description is the canonical lazy-creation failure. PATTERNS.md gets a parallel anti-pattern entry with a fabricated example (e.g., a generic auth or rate-limit task) showing the bad form vs the good form. Then regenerate docs/AGENTS.md, docs/SKILL.md, docs/PATTERNS.md from the templates so committed sample docs stay in sync. NO references to 'ticketwork', 'commitmsg', or any user-specific skill names.

nodes.title: Publish mtix to Docker MCP Catalog
nodes.description: List mtix as a verified MCP server in the Docker MCP Catalog (hub.docker.com/mcp/explore). This gives mtix one-click install in Docker Desktop MCP Toolkit, working with Claude Desktop, VS Code, Cursor, and Windsurf without manual config. Docker signs, builds, and distributes the image as mcp/mtix with container isolation, provenance tracking, and SBOMs.
nodes.prompt:
SCOPE OF WORK

Prerequisites (all met):
- Apache-2.0 license (required; GPL rejected by Docker)
- MCP compliant via mtix mcp (stdio transport)
- Active development, documented, security contact via GitHub issues

DELIVERABLES

1. Dockerfile (in mtix repo root)
   - Multi-stage build: golang:1.25-alpine builder + alpine:3.21 runtime
   - CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath for reproducibility
   - Web UI must be built and embedded (cd web && npm ci && npm run build)
   - ENTRYPOINT ["mtix", "mcp", "--project", "/workspace"]
   - /workspace is the mount point for user project directory

2. server.yaml (for docker/mcp-registry PR)
   Location: servers/mtix/server.yaml in forked docker/mcp-registry

   name: mtix
   image: mcp/mtix
   type: server
   meta:
     category: devops
     tags: [issue-tracking, task-management, ai-agents, llm]
   about:
     title: mtix
     description: AI-native micro issue manager for code-generating LLMs
     icon: https://github.com/hyper-swe.png
   source:
     project: https://github.com/hyper-swe/mtix
     commit: <HEAD commit at submission time>
   run:
     volumes:
       - "{{mtix.project_dir}}:/workspace"
     disableNetwork: true
   config:
     description: Path to the project directory containing .mtix/
     parameters:
       type: object
       properties:
         project_dir:
           type: string
           title: Project Directory
           description: Path to the project containing .mtix/ directory
       required:
         - project_dir

3. tools.json (optional, for catalog display)
   List of mtix MCP tools with names and descriptions, extracted from
   the tool registry. Only needed if Docker build cannot list tools
   without a live project directory.

4. readme.md (for catalog entry)
   Short description for the Docker Hub mcp/mtix page. Can be derived
   from README.md.

VOLUME MOUNT DESIGN

Docker MCP Toolkit pattern: user-configurable single directory mount.
- User provides project_dir in Docker Desktop UI
- Container mounts it at /workspace
- mtix mcp --project /workspace accesses .mtix/data/mtix.db and
  .mtix/tasks.json inside the mounted directory
- disableNetwork: true (mtix MCP needs no network access)
- No secrets needed (local-only tool)

This matches the filesystem and git server patterns in the catalog.

SUBMISSION PROCESS

1. Fork docker/mcp-registry
2. Create servers/mtix/ directory with server.yaml, tools.json, readme.md
3. Run: task validate -- --name mtix
4. Run: task build -- --tools mtix
5. Test locally: docker mcp catalog import catalogs/mtix/catalog.yaml
6. Open PR to docker/mcp-registry
7. Docker team reviews, builds, signs, publishes as mcp/mtix
8. Available in Docker Desktop MCP Toolkit within 24 hours of merge

TESTING

- Build Dockerfile locally: docker build -t mtix-mcp .
- Run with volume: docker run -v /path/to/project:/workspace mtix-mcp
- Verify tools list: echo "{}" | docker run -i -v /path/to/project:/workspace mtix-mcp
- Verify mtix_create, mtix_list, mtix_briefing, mtix_context tools work
- Verify .mtix/data/mtix.db is created/read inside mounted directory
- Verify tasks.json sync works through the mount

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. Dockerfile builds successfully with make build-web && go build
2. docker run -v PROJECT:/workspace mtix-mcp lists all 37 MCP tools
3. task validate passes in docker/mcp-registry fork
4. task build passes in docker/mcp-registry fork
5. PR submitted to docker/mcp-registry
6. Local testing confirms create/list/briefing/context tools work through Docker
7. .mtix/data/mtix.db persists across container restarts via volume mount
8. No network access required (disableNetwork: true verified)
nodes.acceptance: 1. Dockerfile builds and produces working mtix MCP server. 2. server.yaml validates in docker/mcp-registry. 3. PR submitted to docker/mcp-registry. 4. Local testing confirms all MCP tools work through Docker volume mount. 5. Database persistence verified across container restarts.

nodes.title: The board belongs to the repository, not the checkout: git worktrees share one board, and auto-import never lets an older tasks.json overwrite a newer board
nodes.description: mtix finds its board by walking up from the working directory to the nearest .mtix/ (findMtixDir, cmd/mtix/root.go:341). .mtix/tasks.json is tracked in git, so every git worktree and every clone has its own .mtix/ and its own database, loaded by auto-import from that branch's tasks.json. Consequences: (1) a tool or agent that runs mtix in a second checkout (a release-branch worktree, a review worktree, a CI checkout) sees a different, usually stale board: a branch cut before a ticket was created does not have the ticket, and writes made there land on a board nobody else reads. Found while running the HyperSWE review loop against a release/0.5.x worktree: the loop runs mtix in the checkout it works in, so its tracker writes would have gone to the release branch's stale board (worked around with mtix -C). (2) In a single checkout, switching to an older branch and running any mtix command auto-imports that branch's older tasks.json, which can silently revert the board (a known operator hazard).
nodes.prompt: Design first, briefly, in the ticket: (a) for git worktrees of one repository, resolve the board to a single location, e.g. the main worktree's .mtix/ (found through git rev-parse --git-common-dir), with an explicit override (-C and an env var) that always wins; decide what happens to a worktree's own tracked .mtix/tasks.json (ignored for import when it is not the main worktree's). (b) Auto-import must not replace newer board state with older tasks.json content: compare per-node updated_at/content hash or an export generation stamped in tasks.json, and refuse (with a clear message and a --force escape) when the file is older than the database. (c) Separate clones cannot share a directory; document the sync hub as the answer. Touch findMtixDir (cmd/mtix/root.go) and the auto-import path (internal/service sync_service.go AutoImport). Red-first tests: a git worktree resolves to the main worktree's board; -C overrides; an older tasks.json is refused; a newer one imports. Update USERMANUAL, the generated agent docs (claude.md/agents.md templates) and TROUBLESHOOTING (Commandment 15).
nodes.acceptance: 1. Any mtix command run inside a git worktree of a repository uses the main worktree's board unless -C or the env override says otherwise (tested with a real git worktree). 2. Auto-import never replaces a newer board with an older tasks.json; it refuses with a message naming both versions and the --force escape (tested). 3. A newer tasks.json (e.g. after git pull) still imports as today (tested). 4. Separate clones are documented to share state through the sync hub. 5. USERMANUAL, TROUBLESHOOTING and the generated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md sections describe the rule. 6. Red-first evidence and mutation checks recorded on the ticket.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: A rejected create still consumes the parent's sequence number (IDs skip after e.g. 'cannot create child under done parent')
nodes.description: Creating a child under a terminal (done) parent is correctly refused ('cannot create child under done parent X; reopen it first: invalid input', FR-3.9), but the parent's dot-notation sequence counter (sequences table, key '<prefix>:<parent>') has already been incremented and stays incremented. Reproduced on the main board on 2026-09-24: two refused creates under MTIX-95.2 moved its counter 6 → 7 → 8 with no node created. This is why the HyperSWE review loop's follow-up tickets under MTIX-95.2 came out as .2, .4, .6 (each first attempt was refused and burned an ID). CLAUDE.md requires atomic sequence counters in the same transaction as the node write (FR-2.7): a refused create must leave no trace. A plain validation failure such as --priority 9 does not burn an ID, so the leak is specific to checks that run after allocation.
nodes.prompt: Find where CreateNode allocates the sequence (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on sequences) relative to the parent-status check (FR-3.9) and other post-allocation checks in internal/store/sqlite (and the service layer). Make allocation happen in the same transaction as the node insert, after every validation, so any refusal rolls it back. Red-first: a table-driven test that attempts creates refused for each post-allocation reason (terminal parent: done, cancelled; any other check you find) and asserts the parent's sequence value is unchanged and the next successful create gets the next number with no gap. Check the same pattern for micro, decompose and import paths.
nodes.acceptance: 1. A create refused for any reason leaves the parent's sequence counter unchanged (tested per refusal reason, including done and cancelled parents). 2. The next successful create after a refusal gets the next consecutive number. 3. decompose and micro paths covered. 4. Full race suite green. 5. CHANGELOG Fixed entry.

nodes.title: SyncEvent.Validate has no node_id grammar, and SQLite LIKE is ASCII case-insensitive

nodes.prompt: Add a node_id grammar check at sync validation (compatible with ids already on 0.5.x hubs: measure first), and/or make subtree matching case-sensitive (PRAGMA case_sensitive_like or GLOB with escaping). Red-first test with a lowercase id.

nodes.title: Record a rerun --strategy delete as one delete so a single undelete can reverse it

MTIX-95.18 documents per-node recovery; this ticket restores one-step recovery.

nodes.description: Found during MTIX-95.26: import (internal/store/sqlite/import.go about lines 282 and 309) writes an export file's defer_until and other timestamp columns verbatim, without parsing or bounding them. nodes.title: Bound hub push transactions so the late-event sweep's overlap window holds
nodes.description: MTIX-95.5's late-event sweep re-reads hub events created in the last 15 minutes before the previous sweep. That covers push transactions of normal length, but statement_timeout (10 s) limits each statement, not the transaction: a push of up to 100 events can stall mid-transaction (e.g. a laptop suspending while the hub holds the transaction idle), committing events whose created_at is older than the next sweep's window, which the sweep then misses.
nodes.prompt: Bound the push transaction on the hub session: set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout (and transaction_timeout where the server supports it) via set_config for the push transaction (Rule 1a), sized below the sweep overlap. Test with a throwaway Postgres that a stalled push transaction is aborted and its events are not committed; document the bound in SYNC-PROTOCOL next to the sweep overlap.
nodes.acceptance: 1. A push transaction idle longer than the bound is aborted by the hub (tested on a throwaway Postgres). 2. The bound is below the sweep overlap and documented. 3. No provider-specific settings.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Replace-mode import and auto-import drop nodes but keep their events in the local sync log
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.28 dev agent (2026-09-24). clearAllTables (internal/store/sqlite/import.go) deletes dependencies, sessions, agents, nodes and sequences, but not sync_events or applied_events. `mtix import --mode replace` and AutoImport (cmd/mtix/root.go, when tasks.json is newer than the database) use it. If the imported tasks.json predates some nodes, for example one from an older branch, those nodes disappear locally while their create events stay in the log. A later pull cannot restore them: the cursor is already past those events, and the MTIX-95.2 own-event rule acknowledges events the log already holds instead of applying them. The local board then stays behind the hub permanently. This is projection drift in the sense of ADR-006 section 5.3.
nodes.prompt: Reproduce first: on a synced store, create a node, push, restore an older tasks.json that lacks the node, run any command that triggers AutoImport, then pull. Confirm the node is missing and stays missing. Then decide, with the maintainer, how a replace import relates to the sync log. Options: (a) refuse a replace import or AutoImport on a store with sync enabled, and point to `mtix sync pull` or a clone instead; (b) clear sync_events and applied_events and reset the pull cursor in the same transaction, so the next pull rebuilds from the hub; (c) re-derive the missing nodes from the held events. Record the decision in docs/SYNC-PROTOCOL.md. Tests: a table test per import path (import --mode replace, AutoImport) proving the chosen behaviour, including the pull after it.
nodes.acceptance: A red-first test reproduces the lost node. After the fix, no import path leaves an event in the local log whose effect is missing, or the path refuses with a message naming the recovery command. SYNC-PROTOCOL.md, USERMANUAL (import and sync chapters), CHANGELOG, and the sync skill template together with its .claude-plugin mirror describe the behaviour. A doctor check flags any existing drift, and its fix line is a command.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Auto-import and `mtix import` reject mtix's own earlier tasks.json with 'checksum verification failed'
nodes.description: Found while reproducing the annotation export bug (2026-09-24) with a main build on a scratch board: copy .mtix/tasks.json, make one more write (tasks.json is rewritten), then restore the earlier copy, as a git checkout or pull would. The next command logs sync_import_triggered and then 'auto-import failed: checksum verification failed: invalid input'. `mtix import <earlier copy> --mode merge` fails the same way, although the file was written by mtix and never edited. If every restored or pulled tasks.json is rejected, git-based board sharing through auto-import does not work at all. Not yet root-caused.
nodes.prompt: Reproduce with a fresh scratch board (init, create, comment, copy tasks.json, comment again, restore the copy, run any command). Compare computeExportChecksum at write time with VerifyExportChecksum at read time: field set, ordering, omitempty and float formatting (progress, weight), and whether the auto-export writer and `mtix export` share one code path. Fix the cause, add a round-trip test (write, read, verify) over a board with every field populated, and a regression for the git-restore scenario.

nodes.title: Posture refusal and summary count a host the DSN repeats as one host
nodes.description: From the final MTIX-95.25 review (the loop recorded this S3 in its merge receipt without filing a ticket). hostPositions (internal/store/postgres/transport/posture.go) merges consecutive entries with the same host and port. That is right for the driver's own doubling under allow and prefer, but wrong when the DSN itself repeats a host. Count every other entry as a new host. Update the case in posture_host_rule_test.go that pins 'host 2 of 2' for a,a,hidden under verify-full to expect 'host 3 of 3', and add cases for a DSN that repeats a host under disable and under prefer.

nodes.title: A teammate's `mtix dep remove` is refused by the auto-import guard; record dependency removal so descent can be proven

nodes.title: Cloned stores need --project for sync collisions list and sync migrate
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.1.4 round-5 independent reviewer (2026-09-25), end to end with a built binary on a throwaway PostgreSQL hub, and not caused by that change: on a teammate's store created with `mtix sync clone`, `mtix sync collisions list` and `mtix sync migrate` fail unless `--project <PREFIX>` is given, because the cloned store has no local project prefix configured. nodes.acceptance:

nodes.title: sync collisions resolve renumbers locally before the hub accepts, so a refused update leaves them out of step
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.1.4 round-5 independent reviewer (2026-09-25), end to end on PostgreSQL 16 and 17, not caused by that change: `mtix sync collisions resolve` renumbers the losing task locally BEFORE it updates the hub's collision row. When the hub UPDATE is refused (for example a role without UPDATE on sync_node_collisions), the command fails but the local renumber stays, so the local store and the hub disagree about the resolution.
nodes.prompt:
1. Reproduce red-first on a throwaway hub: a role that cannot UPDATE sync_node_collisions runs `mtix sync collisions resolve`; assert today that the command fails AND the local task was renumbered anyway.
2. Fix the ordering so a resolve is all-or-nothing from the user's point of view: update the hub row first (or check the privilege first), and renumber locally only after the hub accepted; if the local renumber then fails, report it with the exact recovery step. Find the code from the `collisions resolve` command in cmd/mtix and its service or transport call; keep all SQL parameterized.
3. Tests for: hub refuses (nothing changes locally), hub accepts (local renumber happens), local renumber fails after the hub accepted (clear message, retry is safe and idempotent).
nodes.acceptance:
- A refused hub update leaves the local store unchanged (test shown failing first on the current code).
- A successful resolve renumbers locally exactly once; re-running it is a no-op.
- USERMANUAL collisions section and the admin skill describe the failure message and the retry.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: sync init re-runs every migration under an exclusive lock and a 30 s deadline, blocking pushes and pulls and failing on large hubs
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.4 round-1 reviewer (2026-09-26), pre-existing: transport Migrate re-runs every embedded migration file in one transaction on every mtix sync init. Migrations 010 and 013 run ALTER TABLE sync_events ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, which takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock even when the column already exists, so every re-run of sync init (after an upgrade, in the restore runbook) blocks all pushes and pulls until the whole migrate transaction commits, including index builds (014, 015). Separately, sync init runs Migrate under the same 30 s context that covers the connect (cmd/mtix/sync_init.go ~101), so on a large hub an index build that takes longer rolls back on every run and the index is never created.
nodes.prompt:
1. Measure on a throwaway PostgreSQL hub with enough rows that the 014/015 index builds take several seconds: hold a migrate transaction open and show a concurrent pull SELECT waits (red-first test).
2. Stop re-running applied migrations: record applied migration files in a hub table (created idempotently) and apply only new ones, or guard each ALTER with a catalog check so a no-op statement takes no exclusive lock. Do not edit the meaning of released migration files; if a guard is needed in an old file, prove the result is identical on fresh and existing hubs.
3. Give Migrate its own deadline, separate from the connect budget, configurable (a config key or flag), and print a clear message naming it when it expires; document what to do when init times out.
4. Docs: USERMANUAL sync init section, docs/SYNC-PROTOCOL.md, the admin skill and mirrors: state exactly what blocks and for how long.
nodes.acceptance:
- A re-run of mtix sync init on an up-to-date hub takes no ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock (PG test).
- An index build longer than 30 s completes when the configured migrate deadline allows it (test with a small deadline).
- Docs describe locking and the deadline truthfully.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: SQL Rule 1/1a: statement_timeout set via fmt.Sprintf, and EXPLAIN queries built by concatenation in a test
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.4 round-3 reviewer (2026-09-26); pre-existing on release/0.5.x and main. Two places break CLAUDE.md SQL Rule 1 / Rule 1a, which allow no concatenation or fmt.Sprintf into SQL, not even for constants or integers: (1) internal/store/postgres/transport/pool.go ~121 runs conn.Exec(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("SET statement_timeout = %d", stmtTimeoutMS)) in AfterConnect; Rule 1a requires SELECT set_config($1, $2, ...) for session settings. (2) internal/store/postgres/transport/late_events_query_shape_test.go ~64-65 builds explainListEventIDsSince and explainFetchEventsByID as "EXPLAIN " + <query constant>.
nodes.prompt:
1. pool.go: replace the Sprintf SET with a parameterized SELECT set_config('statement_timeout', $1, false) (session scope, since AfterConnect configures the pooled connection for its lifetime; say why false and not true in a comment), passing the value as a string such as '15000ms'. Verify on a throwaway local PostgreSQL and through a connection pooler in session mode (and, if available, a hosted provider's direct and pooled endpoints) that the timeout is in effect (SHOW statement_timeout); keep the existing comment's point about startup parameters being dropped by proxies.
2. late_events_query_shape_test.go: keep checking the exact query without concatenation: Prepare the query constant under a name, then run a literal EXPLAIN EXECUTE <name>(<literal args>) statement; or keep a literal EXPLAIN statement and assert in Go that it equals "EXPLAIN " + the constant, sending only the literal to the database.
3. Grep the repository for any other fmt.Sprintf or + building SQL text and list them here; fix those in the same change if they are in the same package, otherwise file them.
nodes.acceptance:
- No SQL text is built by concatenation or fmt.Sprintf in pool.go or late_events_query_shape_test.go.

nodes.title: Import rebuilds sequence counters outside its transaction and can lower them
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.38 developer (2026-09-26): internal/store/sqlite/import.go rebuildSequences runs AFTER the import transaction and rebuilds the sequences table with DELETE plus re-insert of max(seq) per parent. It can therefore lower a counter below a number already handed out (for example a number allocated by a concurrent create that has not inserted yet, or one held by a soft-deleted node if the max ignores it), and a failure between the import commit and the rebuild leaves the counters stale.
nodes.prompt:
1. Red-first: show a counter lowered by an import (a counter ahead of every existing node, then an import, then the counter is lower) and a create that then collides or reuses a number.
2. Move the rebuild into the import transaction and make it monotonic: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE SET value = max(value, excluded.value), counting soft-deleted nodes; parameterized SQL only.
3. Tests for replace and merge imports, and for a rebuild failure (nothing committed).
nodes.acceptance:
- An import never lowers a sequence counter, and the rebuild commits with the import (tests shown failing first).
- CHANGELOG Fixed entry.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: mtix create --type is accepted but silently discarded (issue_type never stored; no way to set it)
nodes.description: Raised by the HyperSWE desk (2026-09-26) and confirmed in code: mtix create accepts --type (bug, feature, task, chore) and silently discards it. cmd/mtix/create.go:156 reads '_ = nodeType // IssueType handled in future refinement.' 4. Docs: CLI_REFERENCE (regenerate), USERMANUAL, the agent templates and skills that mention --type (Commandment 15).

nodes.title: Exec-hook FIFO test: a failure right after Dispatch can race TempDir cleanup
nodes.description: Follow-up from the MTIX-107.23 round-2 independent review (S3, accepted at approval; the loop recorded it only in the merge receipt). In internal/service/hooks_acceptance_test.go, when the test fails within milliseconds of Dispatch, releaseIfParked usually finds no FIFO yet ('no such file or directory', 59 of 60 injected runs). t.TempDir's RemoveAll then races the hook's startup: in 4 of 60 runs the hook's mkfifo or ': >' raced RemoveAll, which added a second failure ('directory not empty') and leaked the temp dir. In the other runs the hook sat about 10 s in open() on the unlinked FIFO and was freed only by a shell-specific SIGCHLD side effect, not by the watchdog, whose path-based write cannot reach an unlinked FIFO. The comment and log text ('the hook's watchdog frees it within 10 s') do not describe that mechanism.
nodes.prompt: Hold the gate by file descriptor instead of by path in the gated hook script: mkfifo "$1" && exec 3<>"$1" && : > "$2"; watchdog: printf '\n' >&3; park: read _ <&3. The watchdog then never needs the path. On a miss after Dispatch (the hook is known to be spawned), retry the release for a bounded time so TempDir cleanup never races the hook's start. Correct the comment and log text. Show it with injected failures right after Dispatch (-count=60): no second failure, no leaked dir, no hook left after the bound; the passing path unchanged; works under dash.
nodes.acceptance:
- 60 injected failures right after Dispatch: exactly one failure each, no leaked temp dir, and no hook process left after the bound.
- The passing path is unchanged; red-again for the flake still fails on the old wait.
- The comments and logs describe the real mechanism.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Renumbering a subtree with non-ASCII ids corrupts the child ids (byte offset in SUBSTR)
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.38 round-4 independent review (2026-09-26); pre-existing, present at base 3474385 (internal/store/sqlite/node_renumber.go:145, now :154). rewriteSubtreeIDs, and rewriteDependencyRefs (~:179), pass len(oldID)+1, a Go byte offset, to SQLite's SUBSTR, which counts characters. For an id containing a non-ASCII character the offset is wrong. Probe: renumbering AA-1é.4 (children .1 .2 .21) to 5 rewrote the children to AA-1é.51, AA-1é.52 and AA-1é.521. Those ids are corrupt and sit in the parent's own namespace, and the ID-counter raise (MTIX-95.38) then set AA:AA-1é to 521. mtix never creates a non-ASCII prefix locally, but pulled node ids are not checked against the id grammar (SyncEvent.Validate checks only project_prefix), so such ids can arrive by sync.
nodes.prompt: In internal/store/sqlite/node_renumber.go, compute the substring offset in SQL (SUBSTR(x, LENGTH(?) + 1) with the old id bound) wherever node ids, parent_id and dependency endpoints are rewritten, as sequence_advance.go does after MTIX-95.38. Red-first with the reviewer's probe (parent AA-1é holding .1 .2 .4 .21; renumber .4 to 5; the children must become AA-1é.5.1, .5.2 and .5.21). Also decide, with a short note on the ticket, whether pulled node ids should be validated against the id grammar at apply (a separate hardening; file it if yes).
nodes.acceptance:
- A renumber of a subtree with non-ASCII ids rewrites every id, parent_id and dependency endpoint correctly (red-first with the probe).
- No other rewrite path uses a Go byte offset with SQLite SUBSTR (grep evidence).
- A decision on validating pulled ids against the grammar is recorded.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: PG-gated cmd/mtix tests flake with a schema-migration deadlock (40P01) in setup
nodes.description: Seen 2026-09-26 while checking the MTIX-95.12 merge result on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16: TestCloudPath_Daemon_PullTickAppliesHubEvents failed in setup with 'migrate: apply schema: ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)' (cmd/mtix/sync_loops_pg_test.go:71 via sync_cloud_paths_pg_test.go:199). - No test weakened; the migration code itself is unchanged unless a real defect is found (then fixed red-first).

nodes.title: Agent docs name 'mtix import --mode replace' as a way out, but main's typed confirmation makes it terminal-only
nodes.description: Found 2026-09-26 while scoping the MTIX-90 backport. On main (176026a), MTIX-90 (4f22aad) gates 'mtix import --mode replace' and 'mtix sync reconcile --discard-local' behind confirmDestructive (cmd/mtix/destructive_confirm.go:134). The operator must type the ticket count at an interactive terminal; --yes and --force do not bypass it, and a non-terminal stdin refuses. The agent-facing docs merged forward from release/0.5.x still name 'mtix import .mtix/tasks.json --mode replace' as a way out an agent can run, without saying it needs a human at a terminal: internal/docs/templates/skills/admin.md.tmpl:73, .claude-plugin/skills/mtix-admin.md:73, troubleshooting.md.tmpl:61 and :69, and the refusal guidance in small-team.md.tmpl:259 and solo.md.tmpl:51 (check the codex mirror too). An agent that follows them gets 'stdin is not a terminal ... Nothing was changed'. That is safe, but the docs are false for this build (Commandment 15: version-matched). On release/0.5.x the guard does not exist, so the same text is true there. This ticket is main (0.6.0) only.
nodes.prompt: On main: find every agent-facing mention of 'import --mode replace' and 'reconcile --discard-local': git grep -n in internal/docs/templates, .claude-plugin/skills, .codex-plugin, USERMANUAL.md, docs/ and the refusal/guidance strings in cmd/mtix and internal/service (the auto-import refusal text, sync_conflict guidance). For each one, say that the command deletes, needs the ticket count typed at an interactive terminal (no flag supplies it), and writes a verified snapshot first; an agent must hand it to the human rather than run it. Where the text offers replace as an agent's way out, point first at the non-destructive route the refusal names. Add a test that pins the rule: every template line mentioning '--mode replace' or '--discard-local' also mentions the typed confirmation or the human. Regenerate the plugin mirrors and CLI_REFERENCE if strings change.
nodes.acceptance: - Every agent-facing mention of a typed-confirmation command on main says it needs the ticket count typed at a terminal and must be handed to the human. - No template tells an agent to run it non-interactively. - A test fails if a template mentions --mode replace or --discard-local without that qualification. - Plugin mirrors are in sync. - Provider-neutral. - CHANGELOG entry under the next main release.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: mtix show's text view omits a deferred task's wake time
nodes.description: Since MTIX-95.22 (release 2513979; also on main), 'mtix defer <id> --until <ts>' stores defer_until, and 'show --json' and .mtix/tasks.json carry it. The text view of 'mtix show <id>' prints 'Status: ⏸ deferred' but not the wake time, so a human or agent reading the text view cannot tell when the task wakes. Verified on a release build of dd15992 (2026-09-26): after 'defer DP-1 --until 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z', show --json has defer_until 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z; the text view shows only the status. Reported from the HyperSWE side while it checked whether a deferral can be restored after a loop run.
nodes.prompt: In the text renderer for 'mtix show' (cmd/mtix/output.go or wherever the Status line is printed), when the node is deferred and defer_until is set, print the wake time in ISO-8601 UTC next to the status, e.g. 'Status:   ⏸ deferred (until 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z)'. When defer_until is absent, print nothing extra. Keep --json unchanged. Table-driven tests: deferred with and without defer_until, and a non-deferred node that still has a stale defer_until (decide and document whether it is shown). Update any doc or skill that shows the show output.
nodes.acceptance: - 'mtix show' text view prints the wake time for a deferred task that has one, in ISO-8601 UTC. - No change when defer_until is absent; --json unchanged. - Table-driven tests cover the cases above. - Docs showing the output updated; CHANGELOG entry.

nodes.title: recover: a table holding two rows with the same id (beyond a damaged index) keeps one silently
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.31.3 developer (round 3, not widened) in internal/store/sqlite/recover_salvage_rows.go (release/0.5.x, once 95.31.3 lands). Salvage walks the primary-key index and reads each row by rowid. Two cases are unhandled when the nodes TABLE itself holds two rows carrying the same id (damage beyond the index): (1) two index entries with that id reaching different rows: salvageRows keeps the last row read and lists the id twice in RecoveredIDs; (2) a row reached through a misread entry that carries id B, when a row is already kept as B: it is not exported again, which is right for the same row, but if it is a DIFFERENT row carrying B, its content is dropped, and the note says only that it was not salvaged again. The export still holds each id once and imports, but data can be lost without a note saying the rows differed.
nodes.prompt: In salvageRows/keepMisreadRow: when a row carrying id B is reached again and its rowid differs from the kept B row's rowid, do not drop it silently. Keep the first, write the second's content to the recovery report (or a side file next to the export) with a note naming both rowids and saying the table held two rows with id B, and list B once in RecoveredIDs. Extend the byte-patching fixture in recover_damaged_index_test.go (or a writable_schema fixture) to build a table-level duplicate, and assert the note and that nothing is lost silently. Update USERMANUAL recovery and the admin skill and mirrors.
nodes.acceptance: - A table-level duplicate id is reported with both rowids, and no content is dropped without a note. - RecoveredIDs lists each id once. - The export stays importable. - Tests cover both cases. - Docs updated.

nodes.title: Hub advisory lock is released with the caller's context and the error ignored

nodes.title: sync --fix doesn't refresh sentinel hashes when content matches
nodes.description: When DB and tasks.json have the same node IDs but the sentinel hash files (.mtix/data/sync.sha256, sync-db.sha256) are stale, mtix sync --fix reports 'In sync' and exits without refreshing the sentinels. The conflict-detection WARN in mtix list persists indefinitely. Reported by external user.
nodes.prompt:
ROOT CAUSE

cmd/mtix/sync.go:58 has:
    if fix && !report.InSync {
        if exportErr := app.syncSvc.AutoExport(ctx, app.mtixDir); exportErr != nil {

The AutoExport (which refreshes sync.sha256, sync-db.sha256, and meta last_export_hash) is only called when InSync=false. But Compare() (sync_service.go:410-479) only checks node ID set equality — it does not read or compare the sentinel files.

So when:
- DB and tasks.json have identical node IDs → InSync=true
- Sentinel hash files are stale (different hash from current content)
- AutoImport conflict detector keeps warning forever

The user runs sync --fix expecting the warning to clear; nothing happens.

FIX

Drop the !report.InSync guard. When --fix is passed, always call AutoExport. AutoExport is deterministic per FR-15.3a (sorted nodes, fixed JSON key order, UTC timestamps) so calling it on equivalent content produces byte-identical output (modulo exported_at). It refreshes both sentinels and the meta last_export_hash. Idempotent.

cmd/mtix/sync.go:58 should change from:
    if fix && !report.InSync {
to:
    if fix {

The user-visible message should reflect both cases:
    if fix {
        if exportErr := ... {
            return ...
        }
        if report.InSync {
            fmt.Println("Sentinels refreshed: tasks.json re-exported.")
        } else {
            fmt.Println("Sync fixed: tasks.json updated from database.")
        }
    }

TESTS (TDD red first)

1. TestRunSync_FixWithStaleSentinels_RefreshesAndClearsWarning
   - Create DB with nodes
   - AutoExport (writes valid sentinels + tasks.json)
   - Manually corrupt sync.sha256 to "stale_hash"
   - Run sync --fix → assert sentinels are refreshed to current values
   - Verify subsequent AutoImport does not warn about conflict

2. TestRunSync_FixWithoutDrift_StillRefreshes
   - Setup synced state
   - Run sync --fix → AutoExport called → exit 0
   - Verify sentinels written

3. TestRunSync_FixWithContentDrift_RewritesTasksJSON
   - DB has node A, tasks.json has node B
   - Run sync --fix → tasks.json now matches DB

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 3 new tests pass.
2. Existing sync tests still pass.
3. Coverage on cmd/mtix/sync.go runSync >= 90%.
4. Manual repro of user scenario confirms warning clears after sync --fix.
nodes.acceptance: 1. Tests pass. 2. Existing tests still pass. 3. mtix sync --fix refreshes sentinels even when content matches. 4. Conflict detection warning clears after sync --fix in user scenario.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Restore a ticket's prior workflow state after an external tool changed it (HyperSWE request)
nodes.description:
Request from the HyperSWE team (2026-09-26, via the desk): when a HyperSWE run is cancelled or declined, HyperSWE wants to put the linked mtix ticket back exactly as it was before the run, including status and assignee (a person's claim).

With mtix 0.5.x verbs it can restore:
- open, or in_progress with an assignee (unclaim, then claim --agent);
- deferred, with `mtix defer <id> --until <ts>`;
- invalidated, with `mtix restore`.

It cannot generically restore a recorded prior state in one audited step. Note that blocked is derived from blocking dependencies (`mtix unblock` re-derives it), so blocked should never be set by hand; it must be re-derived.

For now HyperSWE will report what the ticket was and what it is now, and leave the rest to a person. This is a proposal for a 0.6.0 feature (a minor release; not for the 0.5.x patch line). The maintainer decides whether to build it.
nodes.prompt:
Design and implement (if accepted) a validated, audited way to restore a node's prior workflow state after an external tool changed it.

Suggested shape: `mtix restore-state <id> --status <s> [--assignee <a>] [--defer-until <ts>] --reason <text>`, or an equivalent on `mtix update`.
- It must go through the service-layer state machine: only transitions the state machine allows, with the same side effects as the dedicated verbs.
- blocked is never settable: it is re-derived from dependencies.
- It records an activity entry naming the reason and the actor.
- Reject terminal-state tricks (for example un-cancelling except through reopen rules).

Cover it in CLI, REST, gRPC and MCP per the layering rules, with tests for every valid and invalid transition. Agent-facing docs and a doctor-free verification path are needed per Commandment 15. Coordinate the exact contract with the HyperSWE team through the desk before building.
nodes.acceptance:
- A decision is recorded on this ticket (build or not, and the contract).
- If built: every allowed restore goes through the state machine with its side effects, and blocked is always re-derived.
- If built: each restore writes an activity entry; invalid restores are rejected with ErrInvalidTransition; all four surfaces and the agent docs are updated.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Inbox as the durable inter-agent channel: unbounded wait, retention guarantee, delivery status, full pattern docs (FR-19)
nodes.description: HyperSWE (founder-approved, relayed by the HyperSWE desk on 2026-10-01) is making the mtix inbox the durable channel between its agents: every agent reads its inbox at boot, parks on 'mtix inbox --wait' in the background, and uses a session-start hook with --format context. Four gaps found by that adoption: (1) --wait always times out (default 300 s, exit 5), so callers wrap it in a re-arm shell loop that swallows exit 5; (2) there is no written retention guarantee, and an outage of several days could not be proven lossless (the inbox lives in the sync_events journal in .mtix/data/mtix.db, not in tasks.json, so a tasks.json probe sees nothing); (3) a sender cannot tell whether a recipient acked an event or is alive; (4) the inbox pattern is not documented end to end. Code today: cmd/mtix/inbox.go (runInbox, flags --wait/--timeout/--format), internal/store/sqlite/inbox.go (InboxList, InboxAck, InboxAckThrough, InboxWait), MCP internal/mcp/tools_inbox.go. Prior work: MTIX-47 (FR-19), MTIX-50, MTIX-51, MTIX-55, MTIX-56.8, MTIX-66.
nodes.prompt: Decompose into the four children; each child is self-contained. Follow TDD red-first, the review loop, and Commandment 15 (agent docs ship with each feature).
nodes.acceptance: All four children done through the HyperSWE review loop; the agent-facing docs describe the complete inbox pattern; the HyperSWE desk is told the ticket ids and the release they ship in.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: inbox --wait can block until an event arrives, with no timeout
nodes.description: Today 'mtix inbox --wait' blocks at most --timeout seconds (default 300) and exits 5 on an empty timeout, so a parked agent needs a shell loop that swallows exit 5; otherwise each timeout hands control back to the model and costs a turn. Requested by the HyperSWE desk (founder-approved), MTIX-112.
nodes.prompt: In cmd/mtix/inbox.go (runInbox, flag --timeout) accept --timeout 0 as 'wait with no limit': call app.store.InboxWait in internal/store/sqlite/inbox.go with no deadline, return only when at least one unacked event exists (exit 0) or the process gets a signal (SIGINT/SIGTERM: exit cleanly with a distinct, documented code, never 0, never 5). A negative --timeout is rejected with ErrInvalidInput. Check how InboxWait polls or waits today and make sure an unbounded wait doesn't busy-loop or hold a read transaction or the write lock open. Mirror it in the MCP tool mtix_inbox_wait (internal/mcp/tools_inbox.go) if that tool has a timeout parameter. Edge cases: an event already pending at call time returns immediately; an event delivered by sync pull or a hook during the wait wakes it; the store closing or migrating under the waiter is reported as an error. Clock injected; no time.Now.
nodes.acceptance: Red-first tests: --timeout 0 returns on an event written by another connection after a delay; returns immediately when one is pending; a signal ends it with the documented non-zero code; negative --timeout is refused; no CPU busy-loop (bounded poll count, or a notification). --help and the generated agent docs (claude.md.tmpl, agents.md.tmpl, the relevant skill and its plugin mirrors, USERMANUAL.md, docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md regenerated) document --timeout 0 and its exit codes. CHANGELOG entry.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Written retention guarantee for inbox events, proven by tests across downtime, export and re-import
nodes.description: The HyperSWE desk (founder-approved, MTIX-112) needs a written guarantee that an event addressed to an agent is never dropped or expired before that agent acks it, including when the agent is down for days and when the store is exported and re-imported. Fact today (main bc1f5c1): the inbox is a query over sync_events (internal/store/sqlite/inbox.go InboxList); no code expires or compacts sync_events; only 'mtix sync reconcile --discard-local' (sync_reconcile.go DiscardLocal) deletes it. UNKNOWN and must be established: whether export to .mtix/tasks.json and a re-import (or clone, backup restore, mtix recover, import --mode replace) keeps the journal rows and addressing, and therefore the unacked inbox. tasks.json carries tasks and annotations, not the event journal's addressing.
nodes.prompt: 1) Establish, with tests, what happens to unacked addressed events across: a long gap (no TTL); export then import (merge and replace); backup and restore; clone from a hub; discard-local. 2) Where a path loses unacked events, either preserve them, or refuse/warn loudly and document the loss; file a separate ticket for any fix too large for this one. 3) Write the guarantee, with its exact boundaries, in the docs. 4) Document read-only audit queries a recipient can run to reconstruct what was addressed to it and when it was acked (sync_events where op_type='comment' and payload $.to = <agent>; inbox_deliveries; agent_inbox_ack with acked_at; agent_inbox_cursor), and note that ack --through prunes per-event ack rows below the watermark. Prefer a read-only CLI command (for example 'mtix inbox --agent X --history') over raw SQL in the docs; if you add one, it is in scope.
nodes.acceptance: Tests pin each path in step 1, with the result asserted. The docs (USERMANUAL inbox chapter, generated agent docs, skill and its mirrors) state the guarantee and its exceptions truthfully, including that the journal is per store and reaches another checkout only through sync. Any path that loses an unacked event either keeps it after this change or is refused/warned and documented, with a linked ticket. CHANGELOG entry.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Delivery status for senders: acked or not, and when the recipient last read its inbox
nodes.description: A sender of an addressed comment cannot see whether the recipient acked it, or whether the recipient is alive (last read or parked on --wait), so it waits silently on a recipient that may be down. Requested by the HyperSWE desk (founder-approved), MTIX-112.
nodes.prompt: Design first (a short note as a comment on this ticket, before code): record per agent the time of its last inbox read and whether it is parked now (a heartbeat from inbox reads and --wait, stored in the local store; decide how it behaves across sync, because acks and reads are local to the recipient's store and do not sync today). Then add a read-only query, for example 'mtix inbox status --event <id>' and/or 'mtix inbox status --agent <id>', showing: the event's acked state and time, the recipient's last read and parked state. Expose it over MCP too. State clearly when the answer is only local (the sender's store cannot see another checkout's acks unless they sync), and say what syncing that would cost. Writes through the service layer, in a transaction, with an injected clock. No timers by default (keep scale-to-zero hubs idle).
nodes.acceptance: The design note is posted before the code. Red-first tests for acked/unacked, last-read update on read and on --wait, parked state set and cleared (including after a crash: no permanent 'parked'). CLI and MCP output, --json included. Docs: --help, the generated agent docs, skill and mirrors, USERMANUAL. If cross-store status needs sync changes, those are split into their own ticket and the docs state the local-only limit. CHANGELOG entry.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Document the inbox as a complete pattern in --help and the agent-facing files
nodes.description: The founder asked for the inbox to be documented as a full, copyable pattern so any agent can adopt it (relayed by the HyperSWE desk, MTIX-112). Today it is spread across FR-19 docs (see MTIX-51, MTIX-56.8).

nodes.title: Export node_type asymmetric with import — round-trip not idempotent
nodes.description: MTIX-7 (v0.1.1-beta) made import derive node_type from depth for tamper resistance. But export was untouched and still writes the raw DB column verbatim. So a DB with legacy node_type values (from pre-v0.1.1-beta) exports legacy values; on next import they get normalized — appearing as random 'flips' (e.g., 44 of 140 nodes for a real user). Round-trip is not idempotent. Reported by external user.
nodes.prompt:
ROOT CAUSE

MTIX-7 (commit 7ad4040) added depth-derivation to IMPORT but left EXPORT unchanged.

Import (internal/store/sqlite/import.go:232,255):
    n.NodeType = string(model.NodeTypeForDepth(n.Depth))

Export (internal/store/sqlite/export.go:153):
    COALESCE(node_type, "auto")  -- reads raw DB column

Asymmetry: import normalizes, export persists. So a DB with legacy node_type values exports legacy values; subsequent import re-normalizes them. Round-trip is not idempotent.

User reported: 44 of 140 nodes had node_type flipped after import --mode replace, with the pattern matching depth-derived values (depth 0 → epic, depth 1 → story).

FIX

Make export also derive node_type from depth, matching import. Both ends produce canonical depth-derived values.

internal/store/sqlite/export.go exportNodes(): after scanning rows, override n.NodeType with model.NodeTypeForDepth(n.Depth). Or change the SELECT to not bother reading node_type from DB (just compute from depth in Go).

Cleaner approach — in the loop over rows.Next() after scanning:
    n.NodeType = string(model.NodeTypeForDepth(n.Depth))

This:
- Maintains tamper resistance (export cannot write user-controllable types either)
- Makes round-trip truly idempotent
- Self-heals legacy DBs on next export (one-time migration)
- Matches the symmetry the user is asking for in the bug report

TESTS (TDD red first)

1. TestExportNodes_NodeTypeDerivedFromDepth
   - Insert nodes with intentionally wrong node_type in DB (e.g., depth=0 with stored type=story)
   - Call Export
   - Assert exported node_type = epic (depth-derived), not story (DB value)

2. TestExportImport_RoundTrip_NodeTypeIdempotent
   - Insert nodes
   - Export → write to file
   - Import (replace mode)
   - Export again → assert second export matches first export byte-for-byte (modulo exported_at timestamp)

3. TestExport_LegacyNodeType_NormalizedOnExport
   - Simulate pre-v0.1.1-beta DB state (depth 0 stored as story)
   - Export
   - Verify exported node_type is epic (new convention, depth-derived)

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 3 new tests pass.
2. All existing export/import tests still pass.
3. Coverage on internal/store/sqlite/export.go exportNodes >= 90%.
4. Round-trip from same DB twice produces byte-identical output (modulo timestamp).
5. Documentation: add note to FR-7.8 / FR-15.3a noting that node_type is derived from depth at both export and import.
nodes.acceptance: 1. Tests pass. 2. Existing tests still pass. 3. Round-trip is byte-identical (modulo exported_at). 4. Legacy node_type values normalized on first export. 5. Documentation updated.

nodes.title: Fix v0.1.1-beta tier-swap regression in web UI
nodes.description: MTIX-7 (v0.1.1-beta) swapped depth-to-type mapping (depth 0: story → epic, depth 1: epic → story) for Agile/Scrum convention. Backend was updated. Web UI was missed: ContextChain levelIndicator() still returns OLD letters (depth 0 → S, depth 1 → E), and useFilters ALL_NODE_TYPES still lists story before epic. Every breadcrumb in the UI has been showing the wrong tier letter for many releases. Discovered while investigating MTIX-11/MTIX-12 user bug report.
nodes.prompt:
ROOT CAUSE

MTIX-7 (commit 7ad4040, v0.1.1-beta) swapped the depth-to-type mapping:
  OLD: depth 0 = story, depth 1 = epic
  NEW: depth 0 = epic, depth 1 = story

Backend was updated (NodeTypeForDepth, import.go, node_create.go).
Web UI was missed in TWO places + has a related second bug.

BUGS

1. web/src/components/ContextChain.tsx levelIndicator() — CRITICAL VISUAL BUG
   Current:
     if (depth === 0) return "S";  // wrong — should be "E" (Epic)
     if (depth === 1) return "E";  // wrong — should be "S" (Story)
     return "I";                    // partially wrong — depth 3+ should be "M"
   
   Every breadcrumb badge has shown the wrong letter since v0.1.1-beta.

2. web/src/components/ContextChain.tsx docstring (line 3)
   Says: "S=Story, E=Epic, I=Issue" — STALE since v0.1.1-beta.
   Also missing M=Micro.

3. web/src/hooks/useFilters.ts ALL_NODE_TYPES — MEDIUM
   Currently: ["story", "epic", "issue", "micro"]
   Should be: ["epic", "story", "issue", "micro"]
   Filter checkboxes display in wrong hierarchical order.

4. web/src/types/node.ts NodeType union — COSMETIC
   Currently: "story" | "epic" | "issue" | "micro" | "auto"
   Reorder to: "epic" | "story" | "issue" | "micro" | "auto"
   No behavior change but reflects canonical mental model.

CANONICAL DEPTH-TO-LETTER MAPPING (matches NodeTypeForDepth in Go)
   depth 0 → E (Epic)
   depth 1 → S (Story)
   depth 2 → I (Issue)
   depth 3+ → M (Micro)

FIX (in this exact order)

A. Update ContextChain.tsx:
   - Swap depth 0 and 1 returns
   - Add depth === 2 → "I" explicitly
   - Default → "M"
   - Update docstring to: "E=Epic, S=Story, I=Issue, M=Micro"

B. Update useFilters.ts ALL_NODE_TYPES order: epic, story, issue, micro.

C. Update node.ts NodeType union order: epic, story, issue, micro, auto.

D. Update test fixtures in:
   - web/src/components/__tests__/ContextChain.test.tsx — any assertion that
     expected "S" at depth 0 should expect "E"; "E" at depth 1 → "S"
   - Any other test that uses ALL_NODE_TYPES or NodeType

TESTS (TDD red first)

1. levelIndicator(0) === "E"
2. levelIndicator(1) === "S"
3. levelIndicator(2) === "I"
4. levelIndicator(3) === "M"
5. levelIndicator(7) === "M" (deep)
6. ContextChain renders breadcrumb with correct letter for depth 0 (Epic → "E")
7. ContextChain renders breadcrumb with correct letter for depth 1 (Story → "S")
8. ALL_NODE_TYPES[0] === "epic" (canonical hierarchy first)

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 8 tests pass.
2. All existing TS tests pass after fixture updates.
3. ESLint clean (npm run lint).
4. TS typecheck passes.
5. Manual verification: open the web UI, navigate to a depth-0 node, breadcrumb shows "E" not "S".
nodes.acceptance: 1. All 8 tests pass. 2. Existing TS tests pass. 3. ESLint clean. 4. TS typecheck passes. 5. Manual UI verification: depth-0 node shows E, depth-1 shows S. 6. No regression in Go test coverage.

nodes.title: BYO Postgres backend for shared team workflows
nodes.description: Allow teams to share a single mtix instance by pointing all CLIs at a BYO Postgres database (Supabase, Neon, RDS, self-hosted). mtix OSS deliverable. Builds on existing internal/store/cloud/postgres.go scaffolding from mtix-dev. Solves the team-collaboration scenario without HyperSWE hosting any infrastructure. Per discussion: mtix provides primitives (PG store, audit_log, snapshot command, example hooks, workflow docs accessible to LLM agents); the team owns workflow/policy decisions.
nodes.prompt:
SCOPE

mtix provides reliable primitives for BYO PG team adoption. Workflow/policy decisions belong to the team. Eight deliverables (six original + two from security audit):

1. BYO PG store driver (MTIX-14.1)
2. audit_log table for canonical action ledger (MTIX-14.2)
3. mtix snapshot command with clean failure modes (MTIX-14.3)
4. Three documented reference workflows (MTIX-14.4)
5. Example hook scripts in examples/hooks/ (MTIX-14.5)
6. Agent-accessible workflow recommendations via MCP (MTIX-14.6)
7. Trust model + security documentation (MTIX-14.7) [from audit X1]
8. mtix migrate-to-postgres command (MTIX-14.8) [from audit X2]

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE
- Multi-tenant security model (BYO PG is for trusted teams sharing one DB, not multi-tenant SaaS)
- Hosted PG (HyperSWE premium tier, separate roadmap)
- Server-side hook enforcement (we provide examples, team chooses to deploy)
- CI gating policies (team decision)
- Bidirectional sync (tasks.json is generated, never source)
- Offline write queueing (fail-fast on PG unreachable for mutations)

DESIGN PRINCIPLES

- mtix is a primitive, not a workflow opinion (like git, like postgres)
- PG is canonical source of truth in BYO mode
- tasks.json becomes a snapshot/DR artifact, not the sync source
- audit_log in PG is canonical action ledger; git history of tasks.json is snapshot timeline
- All mutations must be reflected in audit_log atomically with the data change
- Snapshot regeneration is deterministic given store state
- Failure modes are documented and tested
- Trust model is explicit and acknowledged before adoption

TRUST MODEL (must ship in 14.7 before adoption)

Trusted: team members with PG write access, processes on team machines, anyone with the connection string.
NOT trusted: network adversaries (TLS protects), compromised git server (clients talk direct to PG), multi-tenant isolation (out of scope).

CROSS-CUTTING REQUIREMENTS (apply to multiple subtasks)

- TLS defaults to verify-full; refuse sslmode=disable except via explicit --insecure-tls for localhost
- DSN credentials never in tracked config (env var or gitignored .mtix/secrets only)
- Audit_log writes atomic with data mutations (same transaction)
- Backward compatibility: existing v0.1.x SQLite users keep working unchanged
- Test matrix: every store-level test runs against both SQLite and PG (testcontainers-go)
- Coverage: >= 90% on all new code per project standard

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 8 subtasks complete with their own acceptance criteria.
2. Solo (SQLite) workflow continues to work unchanged (backward compat).
3. End-to-end test: 2 simulated CLI processes pointing at one PG, both run mutations, both run snapshot, no data loss, no merge conflict in tasks.json.
4. LLM agent (via MCP) can call a tool to detect setup and receive workflow recommendation.
5. Documentation lives in agent-accessible location (.mtix/docs/) and is regenerated by mtix docs generate.
6. SECURITY-MODEL.md trust model document committed and linked from README.
7. Test suite runs against both SQLite and PG; both green.
8. Total project Go coverage >= 87.5% (no regression from current baseline).
nodes.acceptance: 1. All 8 subtasks complete. 2. SQLite backward compat. 3. E2E concurrent CLI test passes. 4. MCP workflow tool works. 5. Docs at .mtix/docs/. 6. Trust model committed. 7. Both stores tested in CI. 8. Coverage >= 87.5%.

nodes.title: Port and harden Postgres store driver from mtix-dev
nodes.description: Bring internal/store/cloud/postgres.go from mtix-dev into OSS. Audit and harden: SQL dialect cleanup (PG already supports INSERT ON CONFLICT RETURNING, drop SQLite-only PRAGMAs), drop WAL/busy_timeout workarounds (PG MVCC handles concurrency natively), schema migration tool, connection pool config, TLS support (sslmode, sslrootcert for Supabase/Neon), retry/timeout policy for network hops. Connection string in env var or gitignored .mtix/secrets, never in tracked config.
nodes.prompt:
SCOPE

Port internal/store/cloud/postgres.go from mtix-dev into OSS, with security and safety hardening per audit.

DELIVERABLES

A. Driver implementation
   - Implement Store interface against PostgreSQL (modernc-style or pgx-based, decide based on what mtix-dev has)
   - SQL dialect cleanup: PG already supports INSERT ON CONFLICT RETURNING, JSON_EACH equivalent via jsonb_array_elements, advisory locks
   - Drop SQLite-specific PRAGMAs (foreign_keys, busy_timeout, WAL — PG MVCC handles this natively)
   - Schema migration tool with PG advisory lock for single-flight (audit T4 + X3)
   - Connection pool with sane defaults; document pgbouncer for >5 users
   - statement_timeout + connection_timeout configurable, with sane defaults (audit S2)
   - Explicit BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ for export operations (audit S1)

B. Connection security (audit T1, T2, T6)
   - Default sslmode=verify-full; require sslrootcert for managed PG
   - Refuse sslmode=disable unless explicit --insecure-tls flag set AND host is localhost
   - DSN sources: MTIX_PG_DSN env var OR .mtix/secrets file (gitignored, mode 0600)
   - Refuse to load DSN from any tracked config file
   - DSN never accepted as CLI argv (no process listing leak)
   - Test: assert tracked YAML configs with dsn: field are rejected at load time

C. SQL injection regression (audit T3)
   - Re-run the parameterization audit from MTIX-9.1 against PG driver
   - Test cases: malicious values in id, status, type, assignee, priority, label, search query
   - All values bound parameters; no string concatenation
   - JSONB operations use parameterized casts

D. Schema migrations
   - PG advisory lock (pg_try_advisory_lock with deterministic key) ensures single-flight
   - Migrations table records applied versions
   - Mismatch detection: refuse to operate against schema with unknown future version
   - Migration commands logged at INFO

E. last_export_hash redesign (audit X3)
   - Original meta.last_export_hash was per-machine; multi-machine PG breaks the semantic
   - Replace with per-machine snapshot tracking: snapshot_history table (machine_id, snapshot_hash, taken_at)
   - Or eliminate entirely: snapshot operations re-read full state, no skip-optimization needed when PG is shared
   - Decide based on prototyping; document choice

F. Node_type canonicalization in PG (audit X7)
   - Verify MTIX-7/MTIX-12 depth-derived canonicalization works identically in PG
   - Add explicit test simulating legacy data via raw INSERT; verify export normalizes

G. Backward compatibility (audit X4)
   - SQLite remains default
   - PG opt-in via store.driver: postgres in config
   - All existing tests must pass with SQLite store
   - Add parameterized tests for store-level behavior against both backends

H. Least-privilege role recipe (audit T7)
   - Document recommended PG role grants (CREATE on schema only during migration; SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on data tables; no SUPERUSER)
   - SQL recipe in docs

TESTS (TDD red first)

- TestPostgresStore_AllStoreInterfaceMethods (matches SQLite test surface)
- TestPostgresStore_SQLInjectionResistance_AllFilters
- TestPostgresStore_SchemaMigration_ConcurrentSingleFlight (advisory lock)
- TestPostgresStore_SslmodeDisable_RejectedExceptLocalhost
- TestPostgresStore_TrackedConfigDSN_Rejected
- TestPostgresStore_DSNFromCLIArg_Rejected
- TestPostgresStore_StatementTimeout_AbortLongQueries
- TestPostgresStore_NodeTypeCanonicalization_PortedFromSQLiteSuite
- TestPostgresStore_BackwardCompat_DefaultIsSQLite

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 9 tests pass against PG via testcontainers-go.
2. Existing SQLite test suite unchanged and green.
3. golangci-lint clean.
4. New code coverage >= 90%.
5. SQL injection audit confirms all values parameterized.
6. TLS verify-full default confirmed by test.
7. DSN secrets never appear in process listing or tracked files (verified by test).
8. Schema migration concurrency test confirms single-flight via advisory lock.
nodes.acceptance: 1. PG store passes all interface tests via testcontainers. 2. SQLite tests green. 3. Lint clean. 4. >=90% coverage on new code. 5. SQL injection regression passes. 6. TLS verify-full default. 7. DSN never in process listing or tracked config. 8. Schema migration single-flight via advisory lock.

nodes.title: Append-only audit_log table for canonical action ledger
nodes.description: Add an audit_log table (actor, action, node_id, timestamp, before_hash, after_hash) that records every mutation atomically with the data change. Append-only schema (no UPDATE, no DELETE allowed, enforced via PG triggers or RLS). This becomes the canonical action ledger in BYO PG mode — addresses the audit attribution flaw where tasks.json git history attributes Charlies offline mutations to whoever pushes next.
nodes.prompt:
SCOPE

Add an append-only audit_log table that captures every mutation as the canonical action ledger in BYO PG mode. Addresses audit attribution flaw (Charlies offline mtix work attributed to Vimals git push). Designed for safety-critical adoption.

SCHEMA

CREATE TABLE audit_log (
    id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    actor       TEXT NOT NULL,           -- session-validated identity
    action      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- mtix mutation verb (create, claim, done, etc.)
    node_id     TEXT,                    -- target node ID (NULL for non-node ops)
    timestamp   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    before_hash TEXT,                    -- content_hash before mutation (NULL on create)
    after_hash  TEXT,                    -- content_hash after mutation (NULL on delete)
    metadata    JSONB,                   -- structured context (claim agent, transition reason, etc.)
    prev_row_hash TEXT                   -- placeholder for future hash chain (audit S2); leave NULL in v1
);

CREATE INDEX idx_audit_log_node_id ON audit_log (node_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_log_timestamp ON audit_log (timestamp DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_audit_log_actor ON audit_log (actor);

SECURITY HARDENING (audit T1, T3)

A. Append-only enforcement
   - PG triggers: BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE on audit_log → RAISE EXCEPTION
   - Document caveat: superuser can disable triggers; true tamper-evidence requires WAL archival or external append-only store (track in safety-critical workflow doc)

B. Retention policy
   - Configurable cutoff (default 90 days)
   - mtix audit prune --before <date> command archives to .mtix/audit-archive/{date}.jsonl.gz
   - Never silent deletion: prune always logs and produces archive
   - Test: audit_log row inserted before cutoff, prune runs, row archived correctly, file restorable

C. Authenticated impersonation acknowledgment (audit T2)
   - Document in trust model: actor field is logical identity, validated by mtix CLI
   - PG-level user is the real authentication boundary
   - For multi-tenant isolation, use server pattern (out of scope for this ticket)

ATOMICITY (audit S1, CRITICAL)

D. Audit row written in same transaction as data mutation
   - Every Store mutation method (CreateNode, UpdateNode, TransitionStatus, ClaimNode, etc.) must INSERT into audit_log within the same BEGIN/COMMIT
   - Refactor: introduce auditedTx helper that wraps Store transactions and enforces audit row write before COMMIT
   - Failure mode: if audit INSERT fails, entire transaction aborts, user sees error, no orphaned mutation
   - Test: chaos-style — abort transaction at various points after data write but before audit write; verify no committed mutation lacks audit row

SCHEMA CHECK (audit S3)

E. Refuse to operate without audit_log
   - On store init: query for audit_log table existence
   - If absent: error message "audit_log table not found; run mtix migrate to initialize schema"
   - Do not silently skip audit; mtix in PG mode requires audit_log

TESTS (TDD red first)

- TestAuditLog_InsertOnCreateNode_AtomicWithDataWrite
- TestAuditLog_InsertOnUpdateNode_RecordsBeforeAfterHashes
- TestAuditLog_InsertOnTransitionStatus_RecordsActionAndMetadata
- TestAuditLog_UpdateRowAttempt_RaisesException
- TestAuditLog_DeleteRowAttempt_RaisesException
- TestAuditLog_DataMutationCommitFails_NoAuditRow (chaos)
- TestAuditLog_AuditWriteFails_DataMutationRolledBack (chaos)
- TestAuditLog_PruneCommand_ArchivesBeforeCutoff
- TestAuditLog_StoreInitWithoutTable_RefusesWithClearError
- TestAuditLog_BackwardCompat_NotRequiredForSQLite

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 10 tests pass.
2. Schema migration creates audit_log + triggers + indexes atomically.
3. Every store mutation in PG mode writes an audit row in same transaction.
4. UPDATE/DELETE on audit_log raises PG exception (verified by test).
5. mtix audit prune produces restorable archive.
6. SQLite mode unaffected (audit_log not required, no-op in SQLite store).
7. Coverage >= 90% on new code.
8. Trust model caveats documented (superuser can disable triggers).
nodes.acceptance: 1. 10 tests pass. 2. Schema atomically creates table + triggers + indexes. 3. Audit row in same transaction as mutation. 4. UPDATE/DELETE blocked by triggers. 5. audit prune produces restorable archive. 6. SQLite unaffected. 7. >=90% coverage. 8. Trust caveats documented.

nodes.title: mtix snapshot command with clean failure modes
nodes.description: New CLI command that regenerates .mtix/tasks.json from current store state. Deterministic output per FR-15.3a, atomic write per FR-15.3c. Warn-and-skip on store unreachable (does NOT block code pushes when used from a git pre-push hook). Idempotent: same store state produces byte-identical output. Replaces auto-export semantics in BYO PG mode (auto-export off by default in BYO mode; opt-in via config).
nodes.prompt:
SCOPE

New CLI command mtix snapshot regenerates .mtix/tasks.json from current store state. Designed to be safe to call from a git pre-push hook (warn-and-skip on store unreachable, never blocks code push).

CLI

mtix snapshot [--output PATH] [--timeout DURATION] [--strict]

DEFAULTS
- --output: .mtix/tasks.json (per FR-15.1)
- --timeout: 30s
- --strict: false (warn-and-skip on store unreachable; non-zero only on real corruption)

DELIVERABLES

A. Output safety (audit T1, CRITICAL)
   - --output restricted to paths under .mtix/ relative to project root
   - Reject absolute paths outside .mtix/
   - Reject .. components
   - Reject paths that resolve to symlinks pointing outside .mtix/
   - Test: malicious --output values rejected with clear error

B. Snapshot semantics (audit T2)
   - Read store state inside REPEATABLE READ transaction (PG) or single SELECT (SQLite)
   - Document: snapshot reflects store state at the moment the transaction began
   - Same store state -> byte-identical output (modulo exported_at) per FR-15.3a

C. Atomic file write (already FR-15.3c)
   - Write to .mtix/tasks.json.tmp
   - Rename atomically to .mtix/tasks.json
   - Cleanup .tmp on error

D. Failure modes (audit S1, CRITICAL)
   - Store unreachable (PG down, network partition):
     - Default mode: log warning to stderr, exit 0 (does NOT block git pushes)
     - --strict mode: log error, exit non-zero
   - Disk full mid-write: fail, exit non-zero, .tmp cleanup attempted
   - Permission denied: fail, exit non-zero
   - Read timeout exceeded: warn, exit 0 (default) or non-zero (--strict)

E. Bounded execution time (audit S4)
   - --timeout flag with sane default (30s)
   - Read transaction respects timeout via PG statement_timeout or SQLite progress callback
   - On timeout: warn, exit 0 (default) or non-zero (--strict)

F. Idempotency
   - Two calls with no store changes between them produce identical content (modulo exported_at)
   - Test: run snapshot twice, diff output (excluding exported_at field), assert empty

G. Auto-export interaction
   - In BYO PG mode, auto-export is OFF by default (config)
   - Auto-export can be opt-in via config sync.auto_export_enabled: true
   - mtix snapshot is the recommended manual/hook invocation
   - Document this trade-off in workflow docs (MTIX-14.4)

TESTS (TDD red first)

- TestSnapshot_DefaultPath_WritesTasksJSON
- TestSnapshot_OutputAbsolutePathOutsideMtix_Rejected (path safety T1)
- TestSnapshot_OutputDotDotPath_Rejected (path safety T1)
- TestSnapshot_OutputSymlinkOutsideMtix_Rejected (path safety T1)
- TestSnapshot_StoreUnreachable_DefaultMode_Exit0WithWarning (failure mode S1)
- TestSnapshot_StoreUnreachable_StrictMode_ExitNonZero
- TestSnapshot_DiskFull_ExitNonZeroNoPartialFile (atomic write)
- TestSnapshot_TimeoutExceeded_DefaultMode_Exit0WithWarning
- TestSnapshot_Idempotent_SameStateProducesIdenticalContent
- TestSnapshot_DeterministicAcrossPlatforms (FR-15.3a regression)

ACCEPTANCE
1. All 10 tests pass.
2. Default mode is git-hook-safe (never exit non-zero on store unreachable).
3. Strict mode available for users who want hard failure.
4. Atomic write per FR-15.3c (no partial files).
5. Path safety prevents writes outside .mtix/.
6. Coverage >= 90% on new command.
7. End-to-end: simulate pre-push hook scenario, verify code push succeeds even when PG is down.
8. Documentation: snapshot semantics included in workflow docs (MTIX-14.4).
nodes.acceptance: 1. 10 tests pass. 2. Default git-hook-safe. 3. Strict mode for hard fail. 4. Atomic write. 5. Path safety. 6. >=90% coverage. 7. E2E: hook scenario passes when PG down. 8. Snapshot semantics documented.
