nodes.title: Redesign server-side enforcement hooks (pre-receive + GitHub Action) for FR-18 sync model
nodes.description: Deferred from v0.2.0-beta. The v0.1.x server-side hooks regenerated tasks.json from PG-as-canonical-store and rejected drift. FR-18 made local SQLite canonical and PG a replication hub, so that model no longer applies — the git server has no local SQLite to compare against, only the hub. examples/hooks/pre-receive and github-action.yml currently ship as documented no-op stubs (exit 0).
nodes.prompt:
VALIDATE FIRST — do not design until these checks are done:
1. Confirm the stubs are still no-ops: read examples/hooks/pre-receive and examples/hooks/github-action.yml. If someone already redesigned them, comment and close.
2. Confirm there is actual demand: check GitHub issues + ticket comments for users asking for server-side enforcement. If no demand signal exists, comment your findings and recommend the ticket stay parked (the documented alternatives — pre-push hook, daemon-as-service, mtix sync doctor in CI — may be sufficient indefinitely). Do not build speculative infrastructure.

ONLY IF VALIDATION CONFIRMS DEMAND: design constraints to respect — the server can reach the hub (read-only DSN) but has no local SQLite; the check must derive expected tasks.json content from the hub event log (consider: replay events into a throwaway in-memory store server-side, export, compare git-hash against the pushed file). Watch the same-authorID caveat and the cost of full replay on large projects (incremental checkpoint?). Must honor MTIX_SYNC_HOOK-style warn-vs-block semantics and never leak the DSN. Update examples/hooks/README.md 'What's coming in v0.2.1' section, the workflow templates that reference the deferral, and the example_hooks_test.go suite (the PreReceive integration test was removed when the hook became a stub — bring it back).
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Expose --author-id so hub-side conflict logging works across same-machine agents
nodes.description: Deferred from v0.2.0-beta; documented in SECURITY-MODEL.md 'Known audit-trail limitation: same-authorID conflicts'. Vector clocks are keyed by authorID; the emit path defaults every event to authorIDFallback='cli'. Two CLIs sharing that default produce VC-Equal (not Concurrent) events, so the hub's detectConflicts never INSERTs a sync_conflicts row for their concurrent edits. LWW still converges replicas — correctness is intact — but compliance-grade audit visibility of contested edits is reduced. The safety-critical workflow template currently tells operators to set distinct authorIDs 'via direct meta UPDATE during agent bootstrap' because no flag exists.
nodes.prompt:
VALIDATE FIRST — do not implement until these checks are done:
1. Reproduce the limitation on current main: run the e2e conflict scenario (TestE2E_Conflict_SameNodeSameField_LWWConverges shape) with two CLIs sharing authorID='cli' against a local PG and confirm sync_conflicts stays empty; then rerun with distinct authorIDs forced via emitParams and confirm a row IS recorded. If the limitation no longer reproduces (e.g., someone changed VC keying to machine_hash), comment your findings and close.
2. Check no equivalent flag/env already exists: grep for author-id, MTIX_AUTHOR, authorIDFallback call sites.

ONLY IF VALIDATION CONFIRMS: design decision to make explicitly (record in the ticket before coding) — flag per-command (--author-id on create/update/done/etc.) vs one env var (MTIX_AUTHOR_ID) vs config key (author_id in .mtix/config.yaml). Recommendation: env var + config key, NOT per-command flags (agents won't pass a flag on every call; an env var set once in the agent bootstrap is the realistic deployment). Plumb through emitParams.Author (sanitizeAuthorID already enforces the FR-18.7 grammar ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ — reuse it, reject loudly on violation). Update: SECURITY-MODEL 'Known audit-trail limitation' section (the workaround paragraph), safety-critical workflow template step 6 (remove the 'direct meta UPDATE' workaround), USERMANUAL conflict-handling note, MCP-SETUP sync tool description. Tests: unit test for env-var plumbing, e2e test asserting hub-side sync_conflicts row appears when two CLIs use distinct MTIX_AUTHOR_ID, DSN-hygiene sweep still green.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Dedicated perf CI job for MTIX_PERF_LONG-gated threshold tests
nodes.description: Deferred from v0.2.0-beta. All three TestPerf_* threshold tests (Memory_100KNodes, SoloCommandTargets, PushPullTargets) are gated behind MTIX_PERF_LONG=1 because race-detector overhead false-fails their production-calibrated targets in the default CI sweep. benchmarks/README.md documents that 'a dedicated perf CI job that sets the env var (and runs without -race) is the right home' — but no such job exists, so the perf thresholds are currently enforced NOWHERE in CI. A silent perf regression would only surface when someone runs the suite manually.
nodes.prompt:
VALIDATE FIRST — do not implement until these checks are done:
1. Confirm no workflow already sets MTIX_PERF_LONG: grep -r MTIX_PERF_LONG .github/workflows/. If a perf job exists, comment and close.
2. Confirm the three tests are still gated and still pass locally: MTIX_PERF_LONG=1 go test -count=1 ./benchmarks/... (with a local postgres:16 + MTIX_PG_TEST_DSN for the throughput test). If any target now fails on a healthy runner, that is a REAL perf regression — file it as a separate P1 bug before adding the CI job (do not add a job that is born red).

ONLY IF VALIDATION CONFIRMS THE GAP: add a perf job (suggest: in ci.yml as a separate job, or a nightly schedule to keep PR latency unchanged — decide and record rationale). Requirements: NO -race; MTIX_PERF_LONG=1; postgres:16 service container + MTIX_PG_TEST_DSN for the throughput test; -p 1 (PG-gated suites share the database — see the release.yml comment from MTIX-15.13.3); upload benchmark ns/op output as an artifact for trend visibility. Consider gating policy: nightly-with-issue-on-failure is friendlier than blocking PRs on shared-runner perf variance — the thresholds were calibrated on dev hardware; expect to need CI-specific headroom (document any relaxation in benchmarks/README.md rather than silently bumping constants).
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Storage durability: incident remediation (external user DB corruption on full disk)
nodes.description: An external user on v0.1.5-beta suffered unrecoverable SQLite corruption when their disk hit 99% during a WAL checkpoint: main DB truncated (header claims 136 pages, file has 72), WAL subsequently lost, 33 of 80 nodes unrecoverable. Diagnostic bundle at ~/Downloads/mtix-sqlite-corrupted. RCA: docs/incidents/2026-05-19-sqlite-corruption-rca.md. This epic tracks all remediation: durability hardening, redundancy parity for MCP/serve, recovery tooling, fault-injection evidence.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Mirror parity: auto-export tasks.json on every mutation via MCP and serve, not just CLI
nodes.description: Root-cause contributor #1. AutoExport (FR-15.3) only fires in cobra PersistentPostRunE, so it runs once per CLI process. The MCP server (cmd/mtix/mcp.go) and HTTP serve path never trigger it — mutations made by LLM agents (our primary audience) leave tasks.json stale or absent. The affected user had no usable mirror for this exact reason. Fix: trigger auto-export (debounced, e.g. trailing-edge per N seconds or per mutation) after every mutating MCP tool call and HTTP mutation. Add e2e test: mutate via MCP, assert tasks.json reflects it without process exit.
nodes.acceptance: Mutations via MCP and serve update tasks.json without process restart; e2e tests cover both interfaces; export failures surface as MCP tool warnings, not silent log lines.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Fail-stop + pre-flight disk-space checks on all file-resizing operations
nodes.description: Root-cause contributor #2. No code path checks free disk space, and write failures (ENOSPC/EIO) are not classified — some paths warn-and-continue. Fix: (a) pre-flight free-space check on store open and before checkpoint/VACUUM INTO/import/backup, refusing the operation below a configurable threshold with an actionable error; (b) classify ENOSPC/EIO as fatal fail-stop — surface hard error, never continue into subsequent writes; (c) verify (and fault-inject test) that a failed checkpoint NEVER results in WAL reset/deletion — the user's data was recoverable until the WAL vanished; if modernc.org/sqlite resets the WAL after a failed backfill, file an upstream bug and add a guard.
nodes.acceptance: ENOSPC during any write path leaves DB+WAL consistent and recoverable; operations on a near-full disk refuse with clear error; fault-injection tests prove both.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Explicit durability pragmas + fix ADR-001 synchronous drift
nodes.description: Code never sets PRAGMA synchronous; modernc.org/sqlite defaults to FULL (verified empirically, v1.35.0), but ADR-001-STORAGE-ENGINE.md:21 and :45-47 document synchronous=NORMAL — anyone aligning code to the ADR would silently downgrade durability. Fix: set synchronous=FULL explicitly on write connections with a comment explaining the choice; set wal_autocheckpoint explicitly (currently default-1000, undocumented); correct ADR-001; document the durability posture in REQUIREMENTS (new NFR: disk-full safety).
nodes.acceptance: Pragmas explicit in store.go with rationale; ADR-001 matches code; NFR documents disk-full behavior.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Integrity check on open: detect corruption before further damage
nodes.description: QUALITY-STANDARDS scenario #5 (startup integrity check) is declared but unimplemented. The user's corruption was first detected as a hard open failure, after later invocations had already disturbed WAL/SHM. Fix: run PRAGMA quick_check on write-connection open (fast for our DB sizes; benchmark and gate if >50ms at 100K nodes); on failure refuse all writes, print recovery guidance, exit nonzero. Read-only commands may proceed best-effort with a loud banner.
nodes.acceptance: Corrupted DB is detected at open; writes refused; guidance printed; perf budget respected; tests cover truncated-file and corrupt-WAL fixtures.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: mtix recover command + recovery-mode import
nodes.description: No recovery path exists today (migrate is a no-op, verify is diagnostic-only). The affected user's agent recovered 47/80 rows via per-id SELECT with cell_size_check=OFF, but mtix import rejected the reconstructed export because checksum verification has no recovery override (--force only covers zero-node imports). Fix: (a) mtix recover — orchestrates salvage from a corrupt DB: PK-index walk per-id reads, sqlite .recover-equivalent, then merge from tasks.json mirror and backups; emits a salvage report listing what was and was not recovered; (b) mtix import --recompute-checksum (explicit, loud) so reconstructed exports can be loaded; (c) document the full recovery procedure in USERMANUAL troubleshooting.
nodes.acceptance: A truncated-DB fixture (like the real incident) round-trips through mtix recover with all index-reachable rows salvaged; recovery procedure documented and tested.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Automated rolling backups with rotation
nodes.description: mtix backup exists but is manual-only. Add automated backups under .mtix/data/backups/ with rotation: per-session-end and per-N-mutations triggers for CLI/MCP, daily for the sync daemon. Pre-flight space check before VACUUM INTO (depends on the fail-stop ticket); never let a failed backup delete a previous good one.
nodes.acceptance: Backups happen without user action across CLI/MCP/daemon; rotation bounded; restore documented; backup failure on full disk leaves prior backups intact.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Fault-injection test suite: ENOSPC/EIO/kill-9 matrix as release gate
nodes.description: How we missed this: chaos tests cover SIGKILL atomicity but no test simulates environment faults — disk full, EIO, short writes. The honest bar for our robustness claims is surviving kill -9 during every write while the FS intermittently returns ENOSPC. Build: (a) macOS/Linux-portable disk-full harness (small loopback/tmpfs or quota'd sparse image; macOS: hdiutil ram disk filled to capacity); (b) e2e matrix: every mutating command and the MCP server under disk-full, mid-checkpoint kill, and combined; (c) assertions: DB+WAL always consistent or cleanly fail-stopped, mirror intact, no silent continuation; (d) wire into CI as a release gate and publish results.
nodes.acceptance: Reproduces the incident signature (header pages > file pages) on an unfixed build; passes on fixed build; runs in CI; results referenced from QUALITY-STANDARDS.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Claims-to-test traceability: every declared safety scenario maps to a test in CI
nodes.description:
Audit-gap fix. QUALITY-STANDARDS declares 10 safety-critical scenarios; #5 (startup integrity check) and #10 (graceful shutdown WAL checkpoint) had no implementation or test, and nothing detects such drift. ADR-001 contradicted code on synchronous mode. REQUIREMENTS FR-15.3b (auto-export survives disk full) was never tested. Build a traceability matrix (scenario/requirement -> test IDs) checked in CI: a declared scenario without a linked passing test fails the build. Re-audit existing declared scenarios against the matrix. Until the matrix is green, soften public robustness wording.

Update 2026-06-11: scenarios #5 and #11 now exist with tests (NFR-2.8 shipped; e2e/faultinject gates every build) — wire them into the matrix when it lands. Folded in from the pre-push code review: the fault-injection e2e suite currently asserts on error-message keywords (containsAny 'free'/'full'/'truncated' in e2e/faultinject/faultinject_test.go), which is brittle coupling to wording. As part of this ticket, add structured failure signaling — distinct exit codes for ErrDiskFull / ErrCorrupted (and/or --json error output with a machine-readable code field) — and migrate the fault-injection assertions to it. That also gives agents and scripts a stable contract for storage failures.
nodes.acceptance: CI fails when a declared scenario lacks a linked test; all 10 current scenarios mapped or wording amended; ADR/code conformance check added.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: ADR: redundant storage layer — append-only event journal and content-addressed bodies
nodes.description: Evaluate Tier-2 redundancy beyond the tasks.json mirror: (a) append-only .mtix/events.jsonl journal on every mutation (DB becomes a rebuildable index — note v0.2 sync layer already has an event model to potentially reuse); (b) content-addressed body storage (.mtix/objects/<sha>) so prompt/description payloads survive catalog loss as plain text. Both change the storage architecture; write an ADR weighing them against the hardened mirror+backup+recover stack before committing.
nodes.acceptance: ADR with decision, trade-offs (write amplification, locking, GC), and a recommendation; tickets filed for the accepted option.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Agent integrations: Codex and pi plugin targets (issue #15)
nodes.description: Public issue #15 asks for mtix usable from OpenAI Codex and pi (pi.dev) with the same interface as other agents. Findings: (a) Codex has first-class MCP via ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.*] tables (also 'codex mcp add' and project-scoped .codex/config.toml) and natively consumes AGENTS.md, which mtix already generates — support means adding a 'codex' target to 'mtix plugin install' (write/print the config.toml stanza, install AGENTS.md + checklists), a docs/mcp-config/codex.toml snippet, and an MCP-SETUP.md section; docs/codex/AGENTS.md seed already exists. (b) pi deliberately ships NO built-in MCP; it loads AGENTS.md hierarchically (works with ours today) and integrates via TypeScript extensions or the community pi-mcp-adapter extension which proxies MCP servers through a single tool. Tier-1 pi support = documented pi-mcp-adapter setup + AGENTS.md (docs-only). Tier-2 = a native pi TypeScript extension wrapping the mtix CLI (new language surface to maintain — evaluate before committing).
nodes.acceptance: Codex: mtix plugin install codex works end-to-end against a real Codex CLI; MCP-SETUP documents it. pi: tier-1 documented setup verified against pi + pi-mcp-adapter; tier-2 decision recorded (build, defer, or invite community contribution).
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Codex plugin target: mtix plugin install codex
nodes.description: Add 'codex' to mtix plugin install targets. Behavior per existing target conventions: install agent docs (AGENTS.md — Codex's native instruction standard) and provide MCP wiring for ~/.codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.mtix] (project-scoped .codex/config.toml in trusted projects). Never clobber an existing config.toml: write when absent, otherwise print the exact stanza to add. Ship docs/mcp-config/codex.toml snippet and an MCP-SETUP.md section. TDD per TDD-WORKFLOW.
nodes.acceptance: RED-first tests; mtix plugin install codex produces working config + AGENTS.md; existing-config case never overwrites; MCP-SETUP documents it; coverage on new code >=90%.

nodes.title: pi integration tier 1: documented setup via AGENTS.md + pi-mcp-adapter
nodes.description: pi has no built-in MCP by design but loads AGENTS.md hierarchically and supports MCP via the community pi-mcp-adapter extension. Tier 1: add a 'pi' plugin install target that installs the agent docs (AGENTS.md works with pi today) and prints the pi-mcp-adapter setup steps; add MCP-SETUP.md section. Tier-2 native TypeScript extension explicitly out of scope (recorded on MTIX-27).
nodes.acceptance: RED-first tests; mtix plugin install pi installs docs and prints adapter guidance; MCP-SETUP documents the pi path.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Sync: concurrent create-under-same-parent collides; one ticket silently lost
nodes.description: Distributed ID-collision data loss in the FR-18 sync hub. IDs are assigned from the LOCAL sequences table (node_service.go:215 -> store.go:308); the hub assigns no IDs (SYNC-DESIGN s2). Two CLIs that have not yet pulled each other both compute the same next seq under a shared parent and mint the same dot-notation ID (e.g. PRJX-1.4) with different content. At sync: both create_node events carry the same node_id but distinct UUIDv7 event_ids, so the hub stores both (push dedups on event_id only, push_pull.go:63); detectConflicts skips create_node (push_pull.go:148-152) so NO conflict is logged; applyCreateNode does INSERT OR IGNORE INTO nodes (sync_apply.go:393) so the first create_node applied wins and the second is silently dropped. Because the hub gives a total order, all replicas drop the SAME one (convergence holds) but one real ticket's content vanishes with no surfaced conflict. Secondary harms: (a) the losing user's later field-edit events keyed on the same node_id land on the surviving user's node; (b) applying remote creates does not advance the local sequences counter (no sequences write in the apply/pull path), so collisions can RECUR after sync. Scope: concurrent creates under the same parent before either pulls (offline / parallel agents on different machines); single-store parallelism is safe (atomic NextSequence). First deliverable: an e2e reproduction against a real PG hub (also runnable verbatim against Neon). Remediation tiers proposed: (1) stop silent loss - detect node_id collision with a different originating event_id in applyCreateNode, surface as a sync_conflicts row + quarantine instead of INSERT OR IGNORE, wiring into the existing both-renumbered manual action (SYNC-DESIGN line 282); (2) auto keep-both - renumber the incoming node to the next free seq and remap its event stream; (3) advance the local sequences counter on remote-create apply to stop recurrence. Recommend 1+3 first.
nodes.acceptance: e2e repro demonstrates the loss on a real hub (green characterization test, CI-safe, gated on MTIX_PG_TEST_DSN); fix turns silent loss into a surfaced, non-recurring, resolvable conflict; regression test flips to assert both tickets preserved/surfaced.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Security: plugin install follows dangling symlinks (CWE-59 file creation)
nodes.description: MTIX-27 plugin install (internal/docs/plugin_agents.go + shared fileExists in internal/docs/generator.go). fileExists() uses os.Stat, which returns false for a DANGLING symlink (target absent). The write-if-absent paths (installAgentsFile os.Create; installConfigIfAbsent os.WriteFile; also the pre-existing claude-code renderToFile) then proceed and FOLLOW the symlink, creating the file at the symlink's target (proven by direct test: WriteFile through a dangling symlink whose target-parent exists returns nil and creates the victim file). Attack: a cloned/shared repo carries a committed symlink at e.g. .codex/config.toml or AGENTS.md pointing at a user-writable path whose parent exists (git checks out symlinks on macOS/Linux); victim runs 'mtix plugin install --target codex|pi' and a file is created OUTSIDE the project as the victim user = privilege crossing (write-to-repo -> create-file-elsewhere). BOUNDED: (1) cannot OVERWRITE existing files — a symlink to an existing target makes fileExists true and the code skips; only NEW files (target absent) are created. (2) content is NOT attacker-controlled — fixed codexMCPStanza / validated AGENTS.md template — so no RCE/credential injection; impact is unwanted file creation/planting. Severity MEDIUM. NOT in v0.3.0-beta (MTIX-27 merged after the tag). Fix: fileExists should use os.Lstat (a symlink, dangling or not, counts as present -> code skips/manual, never writes through); optionally add O_EXCL on the create as defense-in-depth. The fix is in the shared helper so it hardens the claude-code path too. Add a regression test (dangling symlink at target -> no write-through).
nodes.acceptance: fileExists treats symlinks as present; plugin install never writes through a symlink; regression test with a dangling symlink proves no out-of-dir write; claude-code path covered by the same fix.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Fix SQLite concurrency: busy_timeout on reads + BEGIN IMMEDIATE
nodes.description: Add busy_timeout to read connection and use BEGIN IMMEDIATE for write transactions to prevent database-is-locked errors during concurrent access.
nodes.prompt: In internal/store/sqlite/store.go openDB function: (A) Add PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 for read connections (currently only on write). (B) For write connections, change sql.Open DSN from bare path to path?_txlock=immediate so all write transactions use BEGIN IMMEDIATE. This ensures busy_timeout is always applied (BEGIN DEFERRED bypasses it on lock upgrade). No changes to WithTx in tx.go needed.
nodes.acceptance: 1. Read connection has busy_timeout set. 2. Write connection DSN includes _txlock=immediate. 3. All tests pass. 4. Concurrent mtix show + mtix create does not produce database-is-locked errors.

nodes.title: Distributed node identity (ADR-003): stable dot-path + UID anchor — GA
nodes.description: GA implementation of ADR-003. The dot-path stays the ONLY surface identity (humans, agents, git, all APIs); a UID (= the node create-event id, replica-consistent and PK-unique) is internal only and the visible provisional marker; events key on UID; an eager background claim settles a clean number; the hub registry is a derived uniqueness check (liveness, not a security boundary); restore-induced settled-vs-settled collisions use Option B (detect, fail loud, scoped block, admin resolves, no data loss). Root cause + reproduction: MTIX-28 (e2e/sync_collision_test.go). Full design, decisions, migration phases, agent semantics, the Section 14 security+safety audit, and the scenario matrix live in ADR-003-DISTRIBUTED-NODE-IDENTITY.md. Children are ordered foundation-first; prerequisites are noted per ticket. Every child carries the shared dev rules. DEV RULES (CONTRIBUTING-LLM, TDD-WORKFLOW, QUALITY-STANDARDS, SECURITY-MODEL, ADR-003): TDD red-green-refactor — write failing tests FIRST, confirm RED, add the minimum code to GREEN, then refactor while green. Coverage gate >=90% (storage >=95%) AND scenario coverage: explicitly enumerate and test happy + error + corner + edge cases, never only the best case. Parameterized SQL; all writes transactional; honor the NFR-2.8 fail-stop/disk-full/integrity guards. Godoc on every exported symbol; reference the ADR-003 section/NFR each unit implements. Run /simplify on BOTH the implementation AND the tests and apply the findings. Security+safety: align with the SECURITY-MODEL trust model and the ADR-003 Section 14 audit; run /security-review and the e2e/faultinject suite for any storage/sync change. Commit tests and code together per repo commit rules.
nodes.acceptance: All children done; the MTIX-28 characterization test flipped to assert both concurrent tickets are preserved (no split-brain); traceability gate green for every new safety scenario; /security-review clean; e2e/faultinject + sync-collision suites green against a real hub in CI; USERMANUAL/SYNC-DESIGN/SECURITY-MODEL and agent guidance updated; release-checklist run recorded.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: UID identity foundation: uid = create-event id, stored + indexed, resolver, Phase 0 backfill
nodes.description: Scope (ADR-003 Sec 2, Sec 7 Phase 0, Sec 13): add an internal uid to the node model and nodes table (indexed; never surfaced for settled nodes); define uid := the node create_node event id (PK-unique, replica-consistent — do NOT mint a fresh per-machine UUID); add a display_path<->uid resolver; Phase 0 migration that backfills uid deterministically from each node create event (local-mint fallback ONLY for nodes with no recoverable create event, flagged loudly); make export and the tasks.json mirror carry uid. PREREQ: none (foundation). DEV RULES (CONTRIBUTING-LLM, TDD-WORKFLOW, QUALITY-STANDARDS, SECURITY-MODEL, ADR-003): TDD red-green-refactor — write failing tests FIRST, confirm RED, add the minimum code to GREEN, then refactor while green. nodes.title: RenumberSubtree LIKE patterns don't escape _ and % (cross-prefix id corruption risk)
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-30.13 GA security review (sub-threshold for security, real data-integrity bug). internal/store/sqlite/node_renumber.go builds subtree LIKE patterns as oldID+'.%' / newID+'.%' with ESCAPE '\\' but never escapes '_' or '%'. Project prefixes legitimately allow '_' (projectPrefixPattern), and '_' is a single-char LIKE wildcard. So RenumberSubtree / assertTargetNamespaceFree for a node like DEP_ADD-1 could match an unrelated same-length prefix such as DEPXADD-1.5 when both projects share one local store -> cross-prefix id corruption during renumber. Trigger is a coincidence (same-length prefixes differing exactly at the underscore position, one DB) and only via trusted/operator flows (hub renumber, settle, collision-resolve), so it's not a security vuln under the trusted-team model, but it is real. FIX: escape '_' and '%' (and '\\') in the id prefix before the LIKE, via a small helper, since ESCAPE '\\' is already declared. The 'cloud-validated' assurance is illusory. nodes.title: mtix sync requires a SESSION-mode Postgres connection; transaction-mode poolers break advisory locks + statement_timeout
nodes.description: First real cloud run (Neon via its -pooler transaction-mode endpoint) surfaced hard incompatibilities the Docker-localhost tests never could: (1) TestMigrate_ConcurrentSingleFlight fails 'acquire advisory lock: context deadline exceeded' — the migration single-flight uses session-scoped pg_advisory_lock, which does not work through a transaction-mode pooler (lock holder and waiter land on different backends). (2) TestPool_StatementTimeoutApplied gets statement_timeout '0' not '10s' — the pooler resets the session SET, so mtix's query timeout is not enforced (queries could run unbounded on cloud). (3) The whole transport suite exceeds the 10m default test timeout on cloud (per-test full migrate + network latency + the advisory-lock hang). IMPLICATIONS: mtix sync/migrate against BYO-Postgres REQUIRES a session-mode connection (direct, or a session-mode pooler like Supabase session pooler:5432 / Neon direct). Transaction-mode poolers (Neon -pooler default, Supabase transaction pooler:6543) are unsupported for the migration/single-flight path. ACTIONS: (a) document the session-mode requirement in USERMANUAL/SYNC-DESIGN (which pooler modes are supported per provider); (b) detect a transaction-mode pooler at sync init and fail fast with a clear message rather than deadlocking on the advisory lock; (c) consider a pooler-safe single-flight (advisory-xact lock inside one tx, or a lock-table row) so migrate can work through transaction poolers; (d) bump the cloud test -timeout and tune per-test migration cost. Ties to MTIX-42 (make the cloud gate actually run these).
nodes.acceptance: USERMANUAL/SYNC-DESIGN state the supported connection modes per provider; sync init fails fast with a clear error on a transaction-mode pooler instead of an advisory-lock timeout; statement_timeout enforcement is verified (or documented as pooler-dependent); the transport suite passes against a session-mode cloud endpoint (Neon direct + Supabase session pooler) within a sane timeout.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Sync-applied status changes skip derived-state recompute: sticky 'blocked' in team setups (applyTransitionStatus omits unblockDependents)
nodes.description: Reported by a customer's coding agent: a node stays 'blocked' even though its blockers are resolved (dep show confirms), with no way out — blocked->done is (correctly) disallowed and there is no manual unblock. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): the auto-unblock is wired ONLY into the local mutation path. transition.go:96 calls unblockDependents(ctx,tx,id,author) on any resolving transition (done/cancelled/invalidated), and RemoveDependency/cancel.go do too. But the SYNC-APPLY path internal/store/sqlite/sync_apply.go applyTransitionStatus(~L564) just does 'UPDATE nodes SET status=...' and returns — it NEVER calls unblockDependents (grep count 0 in the file). So when a blocker is resolved on another client and the transition_status event syncs in, local dependents are not recomputed and stay blocked permanently. This hits exactly the distributed/team use case the MTIX-30 epic targets. applyTransitionStatus also omits recalculateProgress (which transition.go runs), so synced status changes likely also leave PARENT PROGRESS stale — verify. blocked is fully system-managed (state_machine.go: blocked->open/in_progress are AutoOnly; only ->cancelled is manual), so when the auto-unblock doesn't fire there is NO manual recovery except cancel. FIX: (1) in applyTransitionStatus, when p.To is a resolving status (isResolvingStatus), call unblockDependents (+ recalculateProgress) inside the same tx, mirroring transition.go — so sync-applied resolutions recompute derived state; (2) add a manual escape hatch: 'mtix unblock <id>' (or 'mtix deps refresh <id>' that re-derives blocked from current blockers) so a stuck node is always recoverable without cancelling; (3) clarify AGENTS.md/USERMANUAL on the blocked lifecycle (auto-managed, how it clears, the recovery command) — the customer agent, lacking this, invented a nonexistent 'documented mtix status is unreliable quirk' and abandoned the status column. NOTE: there is NO such documentation; that claim is false. Audit all sync_apply handlers for the same derived-state-recompute gap.
nodes.acceptance: A blocker resolved on client A and synced to client B auto-unblocks B's dependents (regression test at the sync-apply level, not just local); synced status changes recompute parent progress; 'mtix unblock'/'mtix deps refresh' recovers a stuck blocked node; agent docs explain the blocked lifecycle + recovery; sync_apply handlers audited for other missing recomputes.

Also audit every dispatchApply handler for other missing derived-state recomputes. Being fixed by a background agent on mgit (worktree off fix/MTIX-44, task MTIX-4501); integrates into the MTIX-44 robust fix.

nodes.title: Sync-apply skips content_hash maintenance (stale/NULL hash on synced content edits)
nodes.description: Found during the MTIX-44 sync_apply audit. applyUpdateField/applySetAcceptance/applySetPrompt (internal/store/sqlite/sync_apply.go) skip the content_hash recompute that local UpdateNode runs, so a content edit synced into a replica leaves a stale content_hash (byte-divergent from the emitting replica). Related: applyCreateNode omits content_hash entirely (synced-created nodes get NULL hash) — so the apply path already treats content_hash as apply-derived/non-replicated. content_hash is NOT consumed by sync LWW/convergence, only by import-merge (FR-7.8) and export, so this is not a convergence bug, but it is an inconsistency. DECISION NEEDED: either maintain content_hash consistently across apply (backfill on create + recompute on content updates) OR explicitly document it as apply-derived and recompute lazily on export/import. Contained to internal/store/sqlite/.

nodes.title: Exec-trust: pin the exec target script's content, not just hooks.yaml (trust-on-divergence)
nodes.prompt: The content-hash exec-trust model (internal/hooks/trust.go, ConfigHash) pins ONLY the SHA-256 of hooks.yaml. But the exec adapter (internal/hooks/adapter_exec.go) runs cfg.Command[0] with args, where Command[0] is typically an external script (e.g. wake-agent.sh). That script's CONTENT is outside the trust pin, so editing the pointed-to script runs new code on the operator's machine with NO re-consent -- an approve-then-swap-the-payload escalation that mirrors the approve-then-edit-the-config gap the hooks.yaml pin already closes. Safe for a single-operator repo (only trusted writers touch the tree); matters for the team story where hooks.yaml + scripts are committed/shared and a teammate could alter the script post-trust. Fix options: (a) additionally pin the SHA-256 of each exec Command[0] file at trust time and void trust on divergence; (b) trust-on-first-divergence (re-prompt when a target's hash changes); (c) restrict exec targets to an in-repo, hash-pinned allowlist. Keep exec off-by-default and local-only trust unchanged. Files: internal/hooks/trust.go, internal/hooks/adapter_exec.go, cmd/mtix/hooks.go (trust subcommand).
nodes.acceptance: Editing a script referenced by an exec hook's command voids the local trust (exec no longer fires until re-trusted), verified by a test. hooks.yaml-only edits still void trust as today. Non-exec hooks and the off-by-default posture are unchanged. Trust records remain local + gitignored, never sourced from synced config.

nodes.title: inbox --wait empty-park exit code: field report of exit 0 (seq 209); verify contract + add regression test
nodes.prompt: Field report (seq 209, FR-19 requestor, preview build): 'mtix inbox --agent X --wait' on a FIRST park with an empty inbox returned exit 0 with an empty JSON [] instead of the documented exit 5 (exitCodeInboxEmpty). INVESTIGATION so far: the exit-5 contract IS implemented and correct -- runInbox (cmd/mtix/inbox.go:107-110) returns errInboxWaitEmpty when 'wait && len(events)==0'; exitcode.go:45 maps it to 5; main.go:34 silences its message. Reproduced GREEN (exit 5) on both preview binaries (a393687 and the requestor's 1fe0547) and on current main, for every empty-park variant tried: --timeout 0, -1, 1; JSON and human output; first park after a fresh init. Could NOT reproduce exit 0. HYPOTHESIS: the observed exit 0 is an artifact of the Claude harness reaping a long background CLI park (see the sibling ticket), so the exit code the agent captured was the harness wrapper's, not the CLI's -- not a CLI contract bug. To close: (1) get the EXACT seq-209 invocation (flags, timeout, whether run as a harness background task) and try to reproduce; (2) regardless, add a regression test that pins the contract at the cmd level -- assert 'inbox --wait --timeout 1 --json' on an empty inbox exits 5 and prints [] -- so it cannot silently regress; a store-level InboxWait timeout test already implies it but the cmd exit-code mapping is untested. Files: cmd/mtix/inbox.go, cmd/mtix/exitcode.go, cmd/mtix/main.go.
nodes.acceptance: A cmd-level regression test asserts exit 5 + empty JSON [] for 'inbox --wait' on an empty timeout, in both --json and human modes. If the exact seq-209 invocation reproduces a real exit-0 path, it is fixed and covered by that test; otherwise the ticket documents that the CLI contract is correct and the exit-0 was a harness-reaping artifact (cross-linked to the MCP-wake docs ticket).

nodes.title: FR-19 docs: Claude-agent durable wake path is MCP mtix_inbox_wait, not a backgrounded CLI park (harness reaps parks)
nodes.prompt: Environment finding from the FR-19 field trial (seq 209): a long-running 'mtix inbox --wait --timeout 300' parked as a background process gets REAPED by the Claude harness, so a Claude-based agent cannot rely on a backgrounded CLI park as its durable wake primitive. This is exactly the 'agent that can't hold a socket' case FR-19.5 was designed for: the durable, harness-safe wake path for Claude agents is the MCP tools -- mtix_inbox_wait (long-poll, capped ~60s, RE-INVOKE on empty return), mtix_inbox (list), mtix_inbox_ack -- invoked as ordinary tool calls, not a held process. The CLI --wait primitive remains correct for agents that CAN hold a process (e.g. a shell-loop worker, the aarch64 sandbox). ACTION: document this guidance prominently. Update dist/FR-19-PREVIEW.md (the wake-loop section currently leads with 'mtix inbox --wait' for the worker loop -- add that Claude/harness agents should use mtix_inbox_wait and re-invoke on empty, and that a backgrounded CLI park may be reaped) and the FR-19 feature docs / FR-19.5 section. No code change required unless we also want a doc note in the inbox --wait --help text pointing Claude agents at the MCP tool.
nodes.acceptance: FR-19-PREVIEW.md and the FR-19.5 docs state clearly: Claude/harness-hosted agents should use the MCP mtix_inbox_wait tool (re-invoke on empty) as the durable wake path because a backgrounded CLI --wait park can be reaped; CLI --wait stays documented for agents that can hold a process. No behavioral regression to the CLI.

nodes.title: Hooks: exec fires on the triggering host; daemon-driven dispatch to run exec on a designated host (multi-machine)
nodes.prompt: Field finding (FR-19 exec adapter): hooks dispatch runs in the CLI's post-commit path (PersistentPostRunE -> HooksDispatcher.Dispatch), so adapters -- including exec -- fire on the machine where the triggering mutating command RAN, reading that machine's local journal. Confirmed behavior, not a bug: the exec wake-script executes wherever the CLI happened to post the event. SINGLE-MACHINE topology is fully correct and is the path that matters today -- workers and the poster are the same host, so exec spawns in a working local environment. The wrinkle is MULTI-MACHINE: if machine X posts an event but the wake-script needs to run on machine Y (Y has the toolchain/auth/worker), firing on X is wrong -- observed as an exec that launched but whose spawned action failed because X's environment lacked what the script needed. THE ANSWER (already gestured at -- hooks_dispatch.go:24 notes dispatch also runs 'periodically in the daemon'): daemon-driven dispatch on a DESIGNATED HOST. A dispatch daemon on host Y consumes the journal and fires exec there, regardless of which machine posted the event, instead of exec firing wherever the CLI ran. DESIGN INTERACTIONS to spec: (1) the synced-event guard -- a designated-host daemon must act on events that ORIGINATED elsewhere, i.e. synced events, so those hooks need include-synced (opt-in) while still guarding against every host re-firing; exactly one designated host fires, not all pullers. (2) exec content-hash trust is LOCAL -- trust is pinned on the designated host, so the daemon host is where the operator trusts hooks.yaml (+ MTIX-49's target-script pin if that lands). (3) rate-limit/loop guards move with the daemon. Scope: design + implement daemon-host-designated exec dispatch; keep CLI-local dispatch as the default for single-machine. No change to single-machine behavior.
nodes.acceptance: A designated host can run hook exec dispatch: exec fires on that host for matching events regardless of which machine posted them, with include-synced hooks acting exactly once (the designated host), not once per puller. Synced-guard, local exec-trust, and rate-limit interactions are specified and tested. Single-machine CLI-local dispatch is unchanged and remains the default. No exec fires on a non-designated host when daemon dispatch is configured.

nodes.title: MCP server does not dispatch hooks on mutations — wire Dispatch into the on-commit path (host-side exec cold-start)
nodes.prompt: GAP: hook dispatch (service.HooksDispatcher.Dispatch) is invoked in exactly two places — the CLI post-command path (cmd/mtix/root.go PersistentPostRunE) and the sync daemon's designated synced-dispatch (cmd/mtix/sync_daemon.go, MTIX-52). The long-running MCP server (cmd/mtix/mcp.go runMCP) NEVER dispatches hooks: its only on-commit wiring is wireMirrorExporter (store.SetOnCommit -> tasks.json export + rolling backup), not hooks. CONSEQUENCE: when an agent drives mtix through the MCP server (e.g. a desktop-app local connector running host-side), its mutations commit and mirror, but NO hooks fire — so an exec hook cannot cold-start a worker on the host. This blocks the 'run the mtix MCP server host-side so exec fires there' path (the connector alternative to daemon-driven dispatch, MTIX-52). FIX: dispatch hooks after each committed MCP mutation. The clean seam is the same store.SetOnCommit used by the mirror exporter — register a second on-commit callback that runs app.hooksDisp.Dispatch(ctx) (the LOCAL path: MCP mutations are local events on the server host, so Dispatch, not DispatchSynced). Wire it in runMCP alongside wireMirrorExporter. This gives IMMEDIATE host-side firing (better than the daemon's poll). exec still requires local content-hash trust on the server host (MTIX-49), the per-node rate limit and via-hook guard still apply, and Dispatch never blocks/fails a mutation. Consider whether the same wiring belongs in  (the HTTP/gRPC server) for parity. DESIGN NOTE / posture: this makes a persistent server auto-fire exec on agent mutations — acceptable because exec is off unless locally trusted, but call it out in docs. Files: cmd/mtix/mcp.go, cmd/mtix/mirror_wiring.go (or a sibling), possibly cmd/mtix/serve.go.
nodes.acceptance: A committed mutation made through the MCP server fires matching LOCAL hooks (inbox/webhook/append-file/exec subject to local trust), verified by a test that drives an MCP tool mutation and asserts the hook delivered (e.g. inbox delivery recorded / exec-trusted hook ran). Hook dispatch never blocks or fails an MCP tool call. Rate-limit, via-hook, and exec-trust guards all still apply. tasks.json mirror + backup behavior unchanged. No hooks fire twice for one mutation. Docs note that a host-side MCP server fires local hooks (incl. exec when trusted).

nodes.title: Filesystem-safety preflight: detect unsafe (FUSE/network/virtualized) filesystems and prevent WAL/shm corruption
nodes.prompt: From the 2026-07-11 RCA (preserved in the private design archive). Root cause: a .mtix SQLite DB accessed over a FUSE-passthrough shared folder by concurrent multi-process access corrupts at runtime — SQLite WAL needs true shared-memory mmap of the -shm wal-index plus faithful POSIX locking/fsync, which FUSE/network filesystems do not provide, so processes run on divergent wal-index views (malformed/lost writes). mtix forces journal_mode=WAL unconditionally in internal/store/sqlite/store.go openDB() with NO filesystem-type detection (statfs is used only for free space in diskspace_unix.go). DELIVERABLES: P0 filesystem-safety preflight in Store.New — statfs the DB dir and classify FS type (macOS f_fstypename in {fuse,macfuse,osxfuse,nfs,smbfs,webdav}; Linux f_type magic {FUSE 0x65735546, NFS 0x6969, SMB/CIFS 0xFF534D42, 9p 0x01021997}); on an unsafe FS refuse to open by default with an actionable message naming the FS type and the sync-hub topology, overridable by env MTIX_ALLOW_UNSAFE_FS=1. P1 safe-mode fallback when overridden: journal_mode=DELETE/TRUNCATE + locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE + enforce single-process; never WAL on an unsafe FS. P2 runtime shm probe: detect SQLITE_IOERR_SHM* at open and refuse WAL. P3 observability: log corruption detection and every recover/restore with DB path + FS type. P4 docs: never host .mtix on shared/network/virtualized folders; one local .mtix per sandbox synced via the Postgres hub (FR-18). Files: internal/store/sqlite/store.go, new fsdetect_{linux,darwin}.go, diskspace_unix.go. TDD red-first, >=90% coverage, cross-platform build tags (Linux f_type vs darwin f_fstypename).
nodes.acceptance: 1. Opening .mtix on a FUSE/network/virtualized FS is refused by default with a clear error naming the FS type (test via an injected FS classifier). 2. MTIX_ALLOW_UNSAFE_FS opens in safe single-process mode (journal_mode != WAL, locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE), asserted by PRAGMA. 3. Local disk opens in WAL as today (no regression). 4. Corruption/recover events logged with DB path + FS type. 5. Docs updated with topology guidance. 6. Builds+tests pass on darwin + linux. 7. >=90% coverage on new code; full suite + cloud gate green.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Inbox selective ack (per-event ledger): cumulative watermark drops unacked events on out-of-order processing
nodes.prompt: RCA: the per-agent inbox ack is a CUMULATIVE WATERMARK. InboxAck (internal/store/sqlite/inbox.go) does 'cursor = MAX(cursor, seq)' on agent_inbox_cursor, and InboxList returns events with rowid > cursor. So if an agent processes OUT OF ORDER and acks a higher seq while lower seqs are still unprocessed, the watermark jumps past them and InboxList never returns them again — silent, permanent loss. The at-least-once promise only holds for strictly in-order, contiguous acking; any out-of-order or partial processing drops events. There is also no defer path (an agent cannot mark an event 'seen but not done, redeliver later'). FIX (selective ack via a per-event ledger): add table agent_inbox_ack(agent_id TEXT, event_seq INTEGER, acked_at TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(agent_id,event_seq)). Change InboxAck(agent, seq) to record THAT specific seq in the ledger (idempotent), not advance a watermark. InboxList excludes an event when rowid <= watermark OR rowid is in the ledger (keeps the existing agent_inbox_cursor watermark as a backward-compatible floor + a compaction target). Add InboxAckThrough(agent, seq) for the explicit BULK 'ack everything up to N' case (advances the watermark and prunes ledger rows <= N, bounding ledger growth). Defer = simply not acking (the event resurfaces on the next InboxList). Wire CLI 'mtix inbox ack <seq> [<seq>...]' to selective (multiple seqs), add '--through' for the cumulative case; wire MCP mtix_inbox_ack to selective. Files: internal/store/sqlite/inbox.go, schema.go, cmd/mtix/inbox.go, internal/mcp/tools_inbox.go. TDD red-first; the key test reproduces the drop (ack C selectively, assert A and B still delivered).
nodes.acceptance: 1. Acking a higher seq does NOT drop lower unacked events — InboxList still returns them (regression test reproduces the old drop). 2. InboxAck is idempotent and selective (acks exactly the given seq(s)). 3. Existing agent_inbox_cursor watermarks still hide events at/below them (backward compat). 4. InboxAckThrough advances the watermark and prunes the ledger. 5. CLI 'inbox ack' accepts multiple seqs (selective) + '--through'; MCP mtix_inbox_ack is selective. 6. >=90% coverage on new code; full suite + cloud gate green.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: FR-20: Origin-independent hook dispatch (journal-tail dispatcher + daemon-as-service)
nodes.prompt: Full requirement: the internal FR-20 origin-independent-dispatch spec. Make hook dispatch ORIGIN-INDEPENDENT: a hook fires for a journaled event based only on the event being in the journal and the hook not yet having fired for it on this host — never on who wrote it (local CLI, MCP, REST/gRPC, sync-arrived, or another process). Core: replace the local/synced dual-cursor split with a durable per-(hook,event) DISPATCH LEDGER (exactly-once per host, survives restarts/concurrency/out-of-order — same ledger pattern as MTIX-55 selective ack). One journal-tail dispatch path shared by the daemon (continuous pull-then-tail) and the on-commit trigger (MTIX-53, low-latency local). Fleet exactly-once = hook PLACEMENT (an exec hook lives on the worker host only); include-synced becomes a deprecated no-op. Ship the daemon as an OS-agnostic SERVICE (launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler) via 'mtix daemon install'. Add a global --project/-C <dir> flag on ALL commands. Topology: origin-independence is delivered over the SYNC HUB (each host its own local .mtix), NOT a shared mount (which MTIX-54 refuses as corruption-prone) — the feature must not require a shared filesystem. Crash semantics: at-least-once exec with reclaimable leases (no lost wake; idempotent wake scripts). New-hook backfill guard (intro-floor) so a newly added hook fires only on future events. Claude Code channels: support both — the fabric works channel-free (exec cold-start is the baseline release test); an optional mtix-channel push adapter is an additive follow-up, never a dependency. Release test: a sandboxed poster's addressed comment → the worker host's daemon fires the wake exec → worker cold-starts, zero human touches. Child breakdown + edge/corner cases + scenario tests are in the FR doc §11-14. Build generic (no codenames in code/public docs). To be built by a fable-5 agent, then reviewed.
nodes.acceptance: The release chain works headless on the hub topology: an addressed comment posted on host A fires the wake exec EXACTLY ONCE on the designated worker host B (via B's daemon), does not fire on A, does not re-fire on B restart, and re-fires (not lost) after a crash between claim and fire. include-synced still parses (no-op). Global --project works on non-mcp commands. Daemon installs as an OS service and survives reboot. Filesystem safety (MTIX-54) intact — no shared-mount requirement. Full suite + cloud gate green; >=90% coverage on new code.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Dispatch ledger + journal-tail dispatcher (exactly-once per host)

nodes.title: Safe binary upgrade path: macOS kills in-place-overwritten binaries (SIGKILL/AMFI); daemon KeepAlive amplifies to crash loop
nodes.prompt: Field-hit during FR-20 fleet testing: on Apple Silicon, overwriting an existing mtix binary in place (cp over the file) invalidates the kernel's cached ad-hoc code signature for that inode; every exec is killed with SIGKILL before main (even --version). With 'mtix daemon install' (launchd KeepAlive) the killed binary is respawned forever - a crash loop. Homebrew and go install are safe (new inode/rename); the GitHub-Releases binary-download path has no upgrade guidance. Fix in build+deploy: (1) 'make install' target using install(1) semantics (unlink-then-copy, PREFIX overridable) so the documented path is safe by construction; (2) README Binary Download section: upgrade-safe commands (install -m 0755 / rm-then-cp; never cp over an existing binary on macOS) + note to run 'mtix daemon start' after upgrading so the service picks up the new binary; (3) USERMANUAL 'Upgrading' note under daemon-as-service; (4) RELEASE-CHECKLIST post-release smoke includes the macOS overwrite-upgrade path; (5) 'mtix daemon install' output reminds how to upgrade.

nodes.title: Async exec dispatch: mutation path must not block on hook commands (FR-19 contract fix)
nodes.prompt: Field finding (fleet acceptance run): ExecAdapter.Deliver uses cmd.Run(), which WAITS for the hook command to finish (up to timeout-seconds, default 30s). The CLI post-command trigger and the server on-commit trigger therefore block the mutation path for the duration of a wake script — violating FR-19's 'dispatch runs after commit and never blocks the mutation' contract. Interim field fix: self-detaching wake scripts. Upstream fix (decide before build): spawn the exec DETACHED (Setsid, no wait) and record ledger outcome=delivered on successful SPAWN; the exit code becomes the script's own responsibility (a wake's true success signal is the inbox getting acked, which the fabric already tracks). Rationale: waiting in a goroutine instead breaks in ephemeral CLI processes (parent exits -> outcome stays claimed -> lease re-fire -> systematic double wake). Keep claim-then-spawn ordering so crash-before-spawn still reclaims (at-least-once). hook_log records spawn success/failure; docs + CHANGELOG note that non-zero script exits are no longer visible in hook_log (script should report its own failures). Update the §7 crash-semantics doc and the wake-script template note.
nodes.acceptance: 1. A slow exec hook (sleep 5) adds <100ms to the mutating CLI command and to an MCP tool call. 2. Claim-then-spawn: crash before spawn still re-fires via lease; successful spawn is terminal delivered. 3. Spawn failure (missing script) records outcome=error, never auto-retried. 4. e2e scenario + release-gate tests stay green. 5. Docs/CHANGELOG updated.

nodes.title: Corruption hardening: enforce one-local-.mtix-per-context; detect cross-context/shared-mount access even when local FS looks safe
nodes.prompt: RCA: the internal 2026-07-12 recurring multi-agent corruption report. Recurring structural corruption under multi-agent load: multiple execution contexts share ONE .mtix SQLite DB over a FUSE passthrough (sandbox->host) and write concurrently; WAL -shm shared memory + locking are incoherent across contexts -> orphaned-page corruption. Fingerprint: 17 orphaned .fuse_hidden -shm files + 605KB uncheckpointed WAL. Fleet runs a pre-MTIX-54 build (no preflight). Data fully recovered via mtix recover (45 nodes). ROOT CAUSE is a topology flaw, not a code bug: SQLite is single-host/single-local-FS; sharing one file across contexts cannot be made safe by detection alone. CURE is FR-20 hub-per-host (each context its own local .mtix; share via the Postgres hub). This ticket is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH so a shared-file setup fails LOUD instead of corrupting: (1) verify MTIX-54 preflight ships to all consumers; refusal message must name the hub topology. (2) Multi-opener/cross-context detector: at open + periodically, detect that another context uses this DB even when the local FS looks local -- e.g. .fuse_hidden -shm orphans in the DB dir, or a -shm/WAL from an unreachable owner -- and warn/refuse. (3) Optional lightweight single-writer write-lease sentinel in the DB dir so a second writing context is refused (belt-and-suspenders over SQLite locking that FUSE subverts). (4) Docs: 'one local .mtix per machine/sandbox + hub; never a shared mount' as a first-line adoption rule. TDD; generic (no codenames). Cross-links FR-20 (MTIX-56, the structural cure) and MTIX-54 (the guard).
nodes.acceptance: 1. A shared/FUSE .mtix is refused with an actionable, hub-pointing message (extends MTIX-54). 2. Cross-context concurrent access is detected even when the local FS reports local (test via injected .fuse_hidden/-shm signals). 3. Recover + mirror path documented as the always-available data-safety net. 4. Docs promote one-local-.mtix-per-context + hub as the adoption default. 5. Full suite + cloud gate green; >=90% coverage on new code.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Filesystem preflight: HARD-refuse WRITES on unsafe FS (retire the MTIX_ALLOW_UNSAFE_FS write override); allow read-only for recovery
nodes.prompt: Field evidence: BOTH real corruptions were override-enabled WRITES on a FUSE mount (MTIX_ALLOW_UNSAFE_FS=1). A warning-with-override is a scheduled incident. Change the MTIX-54 policy: on a positively-identified unsafe filesystem (FUSE/network/virtualized), HARD-REFUSE all WRITE transactions with NO override — there is no safe way to write SQLite there (the non-WAL 'safe mode' still relies on FUSE locking, which the field disproved). Keep READ-ONLY access permitted so recovery/query/export still work: 'mtix recover', 'mtix export', read-only queries, and the integrity-bypass recovery path must all still open the DB read-only on an unsafe FS. Repurpose/rename MTIX_ALLOW_UNSAFE_FS so at most it enables READ-ONLY on an unsafe FS (e.g. MTIX_UNSAFE_FS_READONLY) — it must NEVER enable writes. Implementation: in Store.New / the write path, if the FS is unsafe, mark the store write-refusing (every WithTx returns a clear 'writes refused: <.mtix> is on an unsafe filesystem <type>; move it to a local disk / use the hub' error wrapping a sentinel); readers open normally. Remove the non-WAL safe-mode write path added for the old override. Files: internal/store/sqlite/fssafety.go, store.go (openDB/New/WithTx), fspreflight tests. TDD: unsafe FS + write -> refused (no env override re-enables it); unsafe FS + read-only recover/export -> allowed; local FS unaffected. Cross-links MTIX-54 (preflight) and MTIX-57 (cross-context detection). ADR-004 §4.2 (refuse loudly) reinforces this.
nodes.acceptance: 1. On an unsafe (FUSE/network) FS, a WRITE is refused with an actionable sentinel error and NO environment variable re-enables writing (test proves MTIX_ALLOW_UNSAFE_FS no longer opens a write path). 2. Read-only ops on an unsafe FS still work: recover, export, and read queries open the DB (test). 3. Local FS: reads+writes unchanged (no regression). 4. The old non-WAL 'safe mode' write path is removed. 5. Docs updated: unsafe FS = read-only-for-recovery-only; writes require a local disk + hub. 6. Full suite + cloud gate green; >=90% coverage on changed code.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: sync backup: verify-full DSN without sslrootcert fails in pg_dump
nodes.prompt: Found during MTIX-21 cloud e2e. 'mtix sync backup' passes the DSN verbatim to pg_dump. When the DSN uses sslmode=verify-full/verify-ca but names no sslrootcert, libpq's pg_dump looks for ~/.postgresql/root.crt and aborts ('root certificate file does not exist'). Standard libpq behaviour, but a rough edge for cloud hubs (Neon/Supabase DSNs are commonly verify-full). Candidate fix: when the backup DSN requests verification and specifies no sslrootcert, default sslrootcert=system (OS trust store, libpq>=16) for public-CA providers, or emit a clear hint pointing at sslrootcert=system / the provider CA. MTIX-21's cloud test works around this with a test-side helper (pgDumpTrustDSN); the product itself does not yet. Decide: auto-default vs. hint-only vs. docs.
nodes.acceptance: A verify-full/verify-ca hub DSN with no sslrootcert either (a) backs up successfully by defaulting sslrootcert=system for public-CA providers, or (b) fails with a clear mtix-level hint naming sslrootcert=system / the provider CA — not a raw pg_dump root.crt error. Decision (auto-default vs hint vs docs) recorded. Covered by a cmd/mtix test.

nodes.title: Add outgoing webhook support for state change notifications
nodes.description: Generic webhook system for push-based notifications. When a node changes state, mtix fires an HTTP POST to configured URLs. Enables event-driven sync with external tools without mtix knowing anything about Jira/Linear/GitHub Issues.
nodes.prompt:
Implementation requirements from security and performance audit:

Config (.mtix/config.yaml):
  webhooks:
    - url: https://example.com/webhook
      secret: hmac-secret
      events: [node.created, node.done, node.cancelled, node.blocked]
      payload: minimal  # or full

Core requirements:
1. ASYNC delivery — dispatch from event broadcaster goroutine, NEVER inside a DB transaction (WH-01)
2. Minimal default payload: {event, node_id, status, project, timestamp}. Full payload (includes title, assignee) only when payload: full is set (WH-02)
3. HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Mtix-Signature header using per-webhook secret (WH-03)
4. 100ms debounce window — collect events, send as batch array to prevent bulk operation floods (WH-04)
5. Config-file only — not API-configurable (WH-05)
6. Warn at startup if webhook URL is non-HTTPS and non-localhost (WH-06)
7. 5-second timeout per delivery
8. 3 retries with exponential backoff (1s, 5s, 25s), then drop with warning log
9. HTTP client with connection pooling (reuse connections to same URL)

Files: internal/service/config.go (webhook config struct), internal/service/broadcaster.go (webhook dispatch), internal/service/webhook.go (new — HTTP client, HMAC, batching), cmd/mtix/root.go (config loading and validation).
nodes.acceptance: 1. Webhook fires on configured events. 2. Payload matches configured mode (minimal/full). 3. X-Mtix-Signature header present and verifiable. 4. Slow endpoint does not block mtix operations. 5. Bulk decompose (50 children) produces batched webhook, not 50 individual calls. 6. Non-HTTPS non-localhost URL produces startup warning. 7. Failed delivery retries 3 times then logs warning. 8. Config-file only — no API endpoint to add webhooks. 9. Test coverage for delivery, HMAC, batching, timeout, retry.

nodes.title: sync backup: pg_dump mis-parses DSNs pgx accepts (special-char password)
nodes.prompt: Found by MTIX-21's TestCloudPath_Backup on Supabase. mtix sync backup passes the DSN string verbatim as pg_dump's connection arg. pg_dump's libpq URI parser is stricter than Go's pgx: a Supabase pooler DSN whose password contains an unencoded special char (e.g. '@') makes pg_dump mis-split it — 'could not translate host name 123@<host>' — while pgx (used by transport/daemon/conflicts/reconcile) connects fine, so only backup fails. A real user backing up a Supabase/cloud hub with such a password hits this. Fix: parse the DSN once with pgconn.ParseConfig (pgx, which tolerates it) and hand pg_dump the connection via PG* env vars (PGHOST/PGPORT/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/PGDATABASE/PGSSLMODE/PGSSLROOTCERT), invoking pg_dump with NO dsn arg — env values are literal, so no parsing/quoting ambiguity for any password. Extract sslmode/sslrootcert from the DSN query string (after the first '?', so the password span is untouched); fold in the MTIX-59 PGSSLROOTCERT=system default when verify-mode names no trust root.
nodes.acceptance: 1. mtix sync backup connects via PG* env vars, not a DSN positional arg. 2. A DSN with a special-char password backs up (pgDumpConnParams extracts host/port/user/password/database/sslmode/sslrootcert correctly). 3. MTIX-59 sslrootcert=system default preserved. 4. TestCloudPath_Backup green on BOTH Neon and Supabase in the cloud gate. 5. Unit test for the param extraction.

nodes.title: verifyDatabase false-passes a missing backup: reports quick_check ok and creates a 0-byte file
nodes.prompt:
Backup verification can green-light a backup that does not exist.

REPRODUCTION (internal/store/sqlite, package sqlite):
    dir := t.TempDir()
    missing := filepath.Join(dir, "nightly-backup.db")   // NOT created
    verified, err := verifyDatabase(context.Background(), missing)

OBSERVED: verified=true, err=<nil>, and a 0-byte file is CREATED at 'missing'.
EXPECTED: an error, verified=false, and no file created.

MECHANISM — two independently-correct decisions that are unsafe composed:
 1. validateDBFile (internal/store/sqlite/durability.go:90) returns nil for a
    missing file ('absence is the legitimate fresh-DB case'). Correct when
    OPENING a store; wrong when VERIFYING an artifact that must already exist.
 2. verifyDatabase (internal/store/sqlite/backup.go:78) builds the DSN as
    path+"?mode=ro" with no 'file:' URI scheme, so mode=ro is NOT honored:
    SQLite creates the empty file, and PRAGMA quick_check on a 0-byte database
    legitimately answers 'ok'.

EXPOSURE: currently latent. The only production caller is Store.Backup, which
verifies immediately after VACUUM INTO, so the file exists. The risk is that
verifyDatabase is the designated verification primitive — any future caller
that verifies a PRE-EXISTING backup (restore preflight, scheduler health
check, a 'backup verify' command) silently inherits a check that passes on a
missing file. This sits directly behind the 2026-05-19 data-loss incident.

COVERAGE GAP: TestVerifyDatabase_NonExistent_ReturnsError
(internal_coverage_test.go:554) does NOT catch this. It passes only because
its path '/nonexistent/file.db' sits in a directory that also does not exist,
so the open fails for an unrelated reason. It reads as coverage of the
missing-file case while the real case — a missing file in a WRITABLE
directory, i.e. every real backup directory — is untested.

FAILING TEST ATTACHED: branch 'verifydb-false-pass', commit f69d6e9,
internal/store/sqlite/backup_verify_missing_test.go
(TestVerifyDatabase_MissingFile_FailsVerification). The test is committed
RED on purpose and is not merged. Deliberately filed, not fixed.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION (not applied): give the verify path its own
existence precondition rather than reusing the fresh-DB-tolerant
validateDBFile, and build the read-only DSN as 'file:'+path+'?mode=ro' so
SQLite refuses to create a missing file.
nodes.acceptance: verifyDatabase(ctx, path) on a non-existent path in a writable directory returns verified=false and a non-nil error, and does NOT create a file at that path. TestVerifyDatabase_MissingFile_FailsVerification (branch verifydb-false-pass) passes. The misleading TestVerifyDatabase_NonExistent_ReturnsError is either fixed to use a writable directory or kept alongside the new test with a comment stating what it does and does not cover. quick_check-on-empty-file cannot report ok through any verification entry point.

nodes.title: Installed AGENTS.md cross-doc links dangle: every Additional Documentation link is broken
nodes.prompt:
One template renders to two places with different link bases. The generator writes AGENTS.md into .mtix/docs/, where a bare sibling link like WORKFLOWS.md resolves. The plugin installer writes the SAME template to the project root (or a global agent dir), where those links point at files that are not there.

nodes.title: TestAutoExport_Deterministic_SameContent is flaky in CI: Export uses time.Now() directly, bypassing the injected clock
nodes.prompt:
OBSERVED: CI run 32621069742-era and 32625699915 (main, post-MTIX-64.7 merge) failed test-go (ubuntu-22.04) on TestAutoExport_Deterministic_SameContent (internal/service/sync_service_test.go:629-630). Both assertions failed — content AND hash differed between two consecutive exports. Passes 3/3 locally under -race at the same commit, so it is timing-dependent, not a regression from that merge.

ROOT CAUSE: internal/store/sqlite/export.go:139 sets ExportedAt with time.Now().UTC() directly. newTestSyncService injects a FIXED clock into SyncService (sync_service_test.go:38), but that clock never reaches store.Export. Two exports that straddle a second boundary therefore produce different exported_at, so the bytes and the sha256 differ. On a loaded CI runner under -race the package takes ~81s and the two exports land in different seconds; locally they land in the same one.

This is also a CODING-STYLE §10 violation — 'time.Now() in production code' is on the forbidden list, with clock injection as the stated remedy — so the flake is a symptom rather than the whole defect.

BLAST RADIUS: 67 call sites reference .Export(ctx (including tests); 5 non-test callers (cmd/mtix/admin.go, internal/service/sync_service.go x3, internal/relay/bootstrap).

TWO FIXES, needs a ruling:
(a) Thread a clock into Export (signature or a store-level clock field), matching §10. Principled, removes the forbidden-pattern violation, touches a shipped store signature.
(b) Loosen the test to compare content modulo exported_at. Cheap, but leaves the §10 violation and weakens what 'deterministic export' asserts.

Note exported_at is INTENTIONALLY a wall clock — it is why tasks.json shows a diff on every re-export — so (a) means making it injectable, not making it constant.
nodes.acceptance: TestAutoExport_Deterministic_SameContent passes reliably under -race on a loaded runner (verified by repeated runs or an induced delay between the two exports). If (a): store.Export takes its timestamp from an injected clock and no production path calls time.Now() for exported_at; existing export/import tests pass untouched.

nodes.title: CI lint gate is non-hermetic: golangci-lint config verify fetches its JSON schema over the network
nodes.prompt:
OBSERVED: CI run 32625699915 (main) failed the lint job with:
  golangci-lint config verify -> [.golangci.yml] validate: compile schema: failing loading "https://golangci-lint.run/jsonschema/golangci.v2.11.jsonschema.json": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)

Nothing was wrong with the code or the config — the gate reached out to golangci-lint.run for a JSON schema and the request timed out.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT, NOT NOISE: a gate that depends on a third-party host reds every commit on any blip, and a gate that cries wolf trains people to ignore red. That is worse than having no gate, because the next genuine lint failure arrives looking exactly like this one — as it did here, alongside a REAL test failure (MTIX-70) that could easily have been dismissed as 'the usual lint flake'.

It also breaks hermeticity, which the neighbouring CI jobs are explicit about holding: the postgres job's own comment in ci.yml calls out being 'Hermetic — no external secrets'.

LOCATION: .github/workflows/ci.yml lint job (golangci/golangci-lint-action v9.3.0, golangci-lint v2.11.4). The action runs 'config verify' by default; the schema fetch is inside that step.

FIX OPTIONS: pin/vendor the schema locally so verify resolves offline, or disable the network-dependent verify step (the linters themselves run fine offline — 'golangci-lint run' is what actually gates the code). Prefer whichever keeps a config-shape check without the network dependency.
nodes.acceptance: The lint job passes with no outbound request to golangci-lint.run. Verified by reading the job log for the absence of the schema fetch, or by the step being gone. 'golangci-lint run' still gates the code exactly as before, and a deliberately broken .golangci.yml is still caught (or, if config verify is dropped, that trade-off is recorded in the workflow comment).

nodes.title: CI test-go job has no explicit -timeout: internal/store/sqlite runs at ~52% of the 10m default and tips over on runner variance
nodes.prompt:
OBSERVED: CI run 32630584610 (main, post-MTIX-64.8 merge) failed test-go (ubuntu-22.04) with 'panic: test timed out after 10m0s' — FAIL github.com/hyper-swe/mtix/internal/store/sqlite 600.035s. No test failed; the package was killed at the Go default timeout.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM THAT MERGE: MTIX-64.8 added nothing to internal/store/sqlite. In the immediately preceding GREEN run (32627524057, job 97165061864) the same package took 312.878s — already 52% of the 10m budget. Locally under -race it is ~104s. Shared-runner variance of ~2x is all it takes.

NO PATHOLOGICAL TEST: the slowest test in the package is 1.82s (TestEmit_AtomicityUnderKill). The package is simply large — hundreds of tests, each opening a real SQLite store in a temp dir — and -race multiplies it.

ROOT INCONSISTENCY: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 24 is the HEAVIEST test invocation in CI and the only one running on the Go DEFAULT timeout. Every other invocation already carries a considered budget:
  line  89: go test ./internal/store/postgres/transport/ ... -timeout 8m
  line 111: go test ./e2e/faultinject/ ... -timeout=12m
  line 146: go test ./e2e/ -race ... -timeout=12m
So the default was inherited, never chosen.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE RED RUN: a timeout failure looks exactly like a test failure in the CI summary. This is the same cry-wolf class as MTIX-71 — it reds main for a timing coincidence, and it trains people to re-run rather than read. It will recur, because the package only grows.

FIX: give line 24 an explicit -timeout with headroom over the observed 312s, matching the discipline the other three invocations already follow. A budget that still catches a genuine hang (the package DOES complete — this is duration, not deadlock) while not failing on 2x runner variance.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH CONSIDERING SEPARATELY (not this ticket): internal/store/sqlite at 312s under -race is worth profiling on its own merits — most of it is store setup/teardown per test, and a shared fixture where isolation permits would cut it substantially.
nodes.acceptance: The main test-go invocation carries an explicit -timeout, chosen and commented rather than inherited. A run whose heaviest package takes ~2x the current 312s still passes. A genuinely hung test is still killed rather than running to the job limit. Verified by a green run on main.

nodes.title: claude-code plugin target installs root CLAUDE.md with DocsPath-aware links (MTIX-68 pattern)
nodes.prompt:
Extend the MTIX-68 DocsPath fix to the claude-code plugin target, and give that target the root CLAUDE.md it currently never writes.

BACKGROUND — what MTIX-68 established. One template renders to two places with different link bases. The generator writes into .mtix/docs/, where a bare sibling link like WORKFLOWS.md resolves; the plugin installer writes the same template elsewhere, where those links dangle. The fix: templates write cross-doc links as [NAME.md]({{ .DocsPath }}NAME.md); DocsPath is "" for the generator and ".mtix/docs/" for plugin targets, and PluginInstaller copies the data struct before setting it so the caller's generator view is untouched (internal/docs/plugin.go, the pdata/installData copy). agents.md.tmpl was converted; claude.md.tmpl was not.

CURRENT STATE, verified against main today:
- internal/docs/templates/claude.md.tmpl has two bare cross-doc links: line 8 [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), line 60 [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](TROUBLESHOOTING.md).
- CLAUDE.md IS in allDocFiles (generator.go:43), so the generator renders it into .mtix/docs/CLAUDE.md, where those bare links resolve correctly TODAY. Nothing is broken in the generator path.
- installClaudeCode (plugin.go:120) writes skill files and reference files into .claude/skills/ and .claude/skills/references/. It does NOT write CLAUDE.md anywhere. So a Claude Code user gets no root CLAUDE.md from mtix at all — item (2) is additive, not a repair.
- Consequence: today there is no dangling-link BUG for CLAUDE.md, because the only rendered copy is the in-docs one. The links become wrong the moment item (2) lands. Sequencing matters: (1) and (2) must ship together, or (2) alone ships the exact defect MTIX-68 fixed.

SCOPE
(1) claude.md.tmpl: both cross-doc links become {{ .DocsPath }}-prefixed. See the AGENTS.md decision below.
(2) installClaudeCode additionally renders CLAUDE.md at the project root when global=false, using an installData copy with DocsPath=".mtix/docs/". Refuses to clobber an existing CLAUDE.md: loud skip with a named recovery.
(3) docs_path_test.go gains: root CLAUDE.md links prefixed; the .mtix/docs/ copy keeps bare links; clobber refusal pinned. Red-first — each test must be observed failing against current main before the change lands, per the standard set in MTIX-70.

DECISION 1 — CLOBBER POLICY. NOT ambiguous; the house already answered it. installAgentsFile (plugin_agents.go:100) is write-if-absent: an existing file returns Action "skipped" with a Note naming the recovery — 'existing AGENTS.md preserved; regenerate the mtix briefing with mtix docs generate (.mtix/docs/AGENTS.md) and merge what you need'. installConfigIfAbsent uses Action "manual" for the same shape. CLAUDE.md is more likely than AGENTS.md to already exist and to be heavily hand-edited, so write-if-absent is if anything more clearly right here. Follow installAgentsFile exactly, including the Note pointing at .mtix/docs/CLAUDE.md as the always-current copy to merge from. No new policy is being invented.

DECISION 2 — AGENTS.md LINK TARGET. GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS, and the reason this ticket says stop-and-ask. A root CLAUDE.md's [AGENTS.md] link has two plausible targets and neither is right in all cases:
  (a) .mtix/docs/AGENTS.md — always exists once docs are generated, always resolves. But if the user ALSO ran 'mtix plugin install codex' or 'pi', those write a root AGENTS.md (plugin_agents.go: agentsDir = p.projectDir when global=false), and the root CLAUDE.md would then point past the file sitting beside it at a second copy.
  (b) bare AGENTS.md (root) — right when codex/pi was installed, dangles otherwise. Claude Code's own target never writes a root AGENTS.md, so for a claude-only user this dangles always.
The hard part is that install ORDER decides it and templates render once: install claude then codex, and a link chosen at claude-install time is already stale. Detecting a root AGENTS.md at render time makes the output depend on install history, which is the kind of thing that is invisible until it is wrong.
RECOMMENDATION: (a), unconditionally — .mtix/docs/AGENTS.md is the copy mtix owns, regenerates, and can promise exists; it is the only target that never depends on what else the user installed or in what order. Document the choice IN the template's surrounding prose (one line: the mtix briefing lives at .mtix/docs/AGENTS.md and is regenerated by 'mtix docs generate'), so a reader with a root AGENTS.md understands why the link points where it does rather than assuming it is a bug.
DO NOT implement until this is ruled on.

TRACEABILITY: no scenario entry required. docs/traceability.json scenarios 1-27 cover safety-critical behaviour; documentation link resolution is not among them and MTIX-68 added none. The regression tests in docs_path_test.go are the record.

OUT OF SCOPE: the other nine templates' links; the global=true placement (a global CLAUDE.md has no project .mtix/docs to point at, which is a separate question and should not be smuggled in here).
nodes.acceptance: claude.md.tmpl carries no bare cross-doc link. A root CLAUDE.md installed by the claude-code target resolves every cross-doc link from the project root; the .mtix/docs/CLAUDE.md copy resolves every link from .mtix/docs/. An existing root CLAUDE.md is never modified — the install reports a skip whose note names the recovery. docs_path_test.go covers all three, each observed failing before the change. make lint-go clean; internal/docs suite green.
