nodes.title: Pulled events: validate the full envelope per event, quarantine failures, bound Lamport jumps
nodes.description: Pulled events get only format checks; the FR-18.7 caps are enforced by pushers alone. One malformed or extreme hub row is applied (and its Lamport clock adopted), after which the replica's own later pushes fail validation. Separately, any per-event apply error rolls back the whole batch and stalls pull for good: a dependency whose target has not arrived yet, a missing field. Review F-02, M21, census D14.
nodes.prompt:
Pull apply path (cmd/mtix/sync_pull.go; move the logic into the service layer where touched).
1. Before apply, run the FR-18.7 envelope validation with its caps: payload size and depth, Lamport and vector-clock limits, id grammars. Clock-relative checks (the 24h window) are warnings only at ingest (review F-25).
2. Lamport jump bound: config key sync.max_lamport_jump, with a justified default. An event beyond local lamport plus the bound is quarantined and never advances the clock.
3. Per-event isolation: apply each event inside a savepoint. On any error, roll back the savepoint, persist the event to a new local table sync_quarantine (event_id PK, source, raw event JSON, reason, first_seen, last_attempt, attempts, cli_version), and continue the batch. The cursor advances past quarantined events, which stay persisted and are never lost.
4. Retry quarantined events at the start of every pull; a success removes the row.
5. Show the quarantine count in status and doctor (--json).
The local SQLite migration is additive. Coordinate with .2 and .10, which touch the same path.
nodes.acceptance:
Red-first:
1. TestPull_OversizedHubEvent_QuarantinedNotApplied.
2. TestPull_ExtremeLamport_QuarantinedClockUnchanged: the replica's next push still succeeds.
3. TestPull_LinkDepBeforeTargetArrives_QuarantinedThenRetriedAndApplied.
4. TestPull_BatchContinuesPastQuarantine.
5. Status and doctor report quarantined events.

nodes.title: Pull must not re-apply events this client already holds (own-event replay)
nodes.description: `mtix sync pull` fetches every hub event past the cursor, including the client's own pushed events. Effects: a conflict row for every replayed field update whose field has an earlier event (duplicated per pair), and status/claim/unclaim/defer events, which apply unconditionally, revert newer local state. Example: claim, push, done, pull leaves the node in_progress with closed_at still set. ADR-006 D1-D3, S1-S3, S7.

Before mirroring or dispatching: if the event_id already exists in local sync_events (any sync_status), record it in applied_events (INSERT OR IGNORE), merge clocks as today, and return nil with no dispatch and no conflict row. Keep the existing applied_events dedupe. Foreign events must behave exactly as before, including LWW and conflicts. FR-20 journal: no new sync_events row is created, so hooks, inbox and relay publish still fire once per event; document that the Synced flag semantics are unchanged.
Update docs/SYNC-PROTOCOL.md 'Idempotent apply': it claims the originator's applied_events row blocks re-apply, which was never true. State the new rule.
Relay ingest (main only) calls the same IdempotentApply. After merging to main, add a relay regression test: A's event returning to A via peer B is not re-applied.
Reproduction pattern (see internal-docs/repro): emit through real store mutations, read the pending projection as the hub stores it, mark it pushed, and feed the same events back through IdempotentApply.

nodes.title: Hardening follow-up (0.5.4): out-of-range event timestamps can make nodes unreadable
nodes.description: A synced event's wall_clock_ts is only checked for being non-negative (model.Validate). MTIX-95.10 (round 2) guards its own new use (closed_at of a winning workflow event falls back to the apply time). The MTIX-95.10 dev agent reported that applyComment stamps an annotation's CreatedAt and the node's updated_at from wall_clock_ts too (pre-existing, untested), so a single comment event from a buggy clock or a hostile hub member can make a node, and every list that includes it, unreadable on all replicas.

Fix at the boundary: reject or bound out-of-range wall_clock_ts at ingest (this belongs with MTIX-95.11's envelope validation: an out-of-range wall_clock_ts is quarantined there once 95.11 lands; until then, fall back to the apply time as 95.10 does, one shared helper). 3. Audit every other use of wall_clock_ts in internal/store/sqlite apply code for the same pattern and cover each with a test. Unpublished robustness fix: neutral commit/CHANGELOG wording ('Hardening (MTIX-95.x).'); run on the sec/0.5.4 lane or coordinate with 95.11 on release/0.5.x.

nodes.title: Push must acknowledge events already on the hub (no permanently pending queue)
nodes.description: The hub reports an event as accepted only when its INSERT affects a row (push_pull.go, RowsAffected==1). An event that reached the hub but whose local 'pushed' mark was lost stays pending forever. That happens when the commit acknowledgement is lost, the process crashes or the disk fails before markPushed, or a retry follows a network drop. Pending events are read lowest-Lamport first, 100 per batch, and pushLoop stops when a batch accepts nothing. Once a full batch of such events sits at the head of the queue, nothing behind it is ever pushed, while push still reports success. ADR-006 D7.

ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING`, if no row was inserted, check whether the event_id is present on the hub. Batch this with ANY($1) to keep one round trip per batch. Report present events as accepted so the client marks them pushed. Renumber, collision and same-node no-op semantics are unchanged. The progress line distinguishes inserted from already-present.

nodes.title: Verify: first pull after upgrading 0.5.3 to 0.5.4 may be refused as a false conflict (baseline hashed in the old export format)
nodes.description:
Raised by the MTIX-95.31.9 round-4 independent reviewer (2026-09-25) as likely but NOT verified: v0.5.3 writes the FR-15.2h conflict baseline (.mtix/data/sync-db.sha256) as a hash of its 1.0.0-format export, while 0.5.4 (MTIX-95.31.1) hashes a 2.0.0-format export (every annotation and node column). If the baseline is compared across that change, the first automatic import after upgrading a store from 0.5.3 to 0.5.4, before any local write, may be refused as "both the local store and tasks.json changed", for every user who upgrades, although nothing changed.

The same review found a narrower case inside 95.31.9 (a baseline written while the store held uid-less tasks, then the open-time backfill mints uids): that one is filed by the loop as an S3 follow-up of MTIX-95.31.9.

The MTIX-95.31.4 reply says upgrades from v0.3.0 and v0.5.3 were exercised end to end; check whether that run covered this exact order (upgrade, then a pull that changed tasks.json, with no local write in between).
nodes.prompt:
1. Reproduce with real binaries in a scratch directory (never replace an installed mtix): build or download v0.5.3, create a store, make a few tasks with annotations, let it write tasks.json and its baseline. Then, with a 0.5.4 build from release/0.5.x: (a) run a read-only command, then pull a teammate's changed tasks.json (git pull of the file) and trigger the auto-import; (b) the same with no command before the pull. Record exactly what each prints and whether the import applies or is refused.
2. If the import is refused, the fix: on the first open by a binary whose export format differs from the one that wrote the baseline, recompute the baseline from the current store in the new format before any comparison, but only when the store matches the old baseline under the old format (so a real local change is still detected). Keep the check inside the existing auto-import guard (internal/service/sync_autoimport_guard.go and the baseline helpers). Red-first with a fixture baseline in the 1.0.0 format.
3. If it is not refused, record the evidence here and close the ticket as verified.
nodes.acceptance:
- A recorded run with a real v0.5.3 store and a 0.5.4 build shows the first pull after upgrading applies a teammate's change without a false conflict refusal, both with and without a command before the pull.
- A real local change made before the upgrade is still detected as a conflict.
- If code changed: a red-first test with a 1.0.0-format baseline fixture, CHANGELOG Fixed entry, and the USERMANUAL upgrade notes.

nodes.title: First pull after upgrading from 0.5.3 or older is refused as lossy for history an older board never carried
nodes.description:
Found by the MTIX-95.31.11 round-3 independent review (2026-09-26), reproduced with real v0.5.3-beta and v0.3.0-beta binaries. It is adjacent to that change: MTIX-95.31.11 removes the false conflict on the first pull after an upgrade, and this refusal comes after that step.

Sequence:
1. On 0.5.3, A claims PROJ-1 and pushes. Teammate B pulls on 0.5.3.
2. B upgrades to 0.5.4 and claims PROJ-2.
3. A upgrades and pulls.

The baseline is recognized (sync_baseline_upgraded from_form=1.0.0), then the import is refused as lossy: "PROJ-1: 1 activity entry". B's board could never carry that entry, because the 1.0.0 export form never exported activity. The same refusal happens when upgrading from 0.3.0 and on a larger 0.5.3 store (activity, previous_status, deleted_by).

The documented "To choose" advice (a client older than 0.5.4: ask the teammate to upgrade) does not fit, because the teammate did upgrade. The only way out that keeps the data, a merge import, reverts B's claim (MTIX-95.31.13). So most teams upgrading from 0.5.3 hit a refused first pull with no clean way out.
nodes.prompt:
1. Write a short design note in the ticket (a comment) first. It covers the loss check in the automatic import (internal/service, the import loss check). Decide how it should treat local-only activity entries and task fields (activity, previous_status, deleted_by, and any other field the 1.0.0 export form did not carry) when the pulled board could not have carried them. Options to weigh:
   - (a) Keep local-only history that the incoming board's form cannot represent: merge it into the store rather than counting it as lost.
   - (b) Do not count such items as a loss when the board or the baseline is in, or descends from, a pre-0.5.4 form.
   - (c) Keep refusing, but print a precise, safe way out.
   Prefer an option that never silently drops a user's annotations or task content, and never reverts a teammate's status or assignee change.
2. Implement it red-first with real-binary fixtures: v0.5.3-beta and v0.3.0-beta stores, the sequence in the description, a larger 0.5.3 store, and controls where a genuine local loss (a comment the board lacks) must still be refused.
3. Update the USERMANUAL upgrade notes (the "first pull after the upgrade" text), CHANGELOG, internal/docs/templates/troubleshooting.md.tmpl and the admin skill with its .claude-plugin and .codex-plugin mirrors (Commandment 15).
nodes.acceptance:
- The upgrade sequence in the description (and the 0.3.0 and larger-0.5.3 variants) imports on the first pull after upgrading: the teammate's claim is applied, and no local annotation or task content is lost (red-first with real-binary fixtures).
- A genuine local loss (a comment or task content the board lacks) is still refused.
- The design note is recorded on this ticket.
- The docs describe the upgrade path truthfully (USERMANUAL, CHANGELOG, troubleshooting template, admin skill and mirrors).
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: A uid adopted by a merge import is not carried onto the task's unpushed sync events
nodes.description:
Found by the MTIX-95.12 run-2 independent review (2026-09-26), reproduced on a real hub (PostgreSQL 16 and 17).

When a merge import (explicit `--mode merge`, or the automatic import after a git pull) adopts the file's uid for a local task (MTIX-95.31.6; since MTIX-95.31.9 a marked backfill uid counts as one assigned later), the task's pending, not yet pushed sync_events keep the OLD uid. A held creation (MTIX-95.12) keeps it too. Every later change carries the NEW uid.

A later push, or the release of a held creation, can therefore send one task's creation and its later changes under different uids. The hub then applies them to different identities: on the real hub, a teammate's task took the local title, and a local child appeared under the teammate's task.

MTIX-95.12 run 2 adds a conservative push-side hold so nothing is sent while the creation is held. The adoption itself should keep a task's unpushed events consistent with the task's identity.
nodes.acceptance:
- After a merge adopts a uid, no push or release sends one task's events under two different uids (tested red-first on a fake hub and on a real hub, PG16 and PG17).
- A teammate's task is never modified by another task's events.
- The docs describe the adoption's effect on unpushed changes.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Relay peers keep a task's old uid when a merge import adopts a uid after the event was published to the relay
nodes.description: From the MTIX-95.31.16 review (2026-10-01): the FR-21 relay publishes sync_events by rowid (relay_cursor.go:234) and keeps its own cursor. When a merge import adopts a uid, the carry rewrites pending events' uid and creation id in place; an event already framed to the relay keeps the old uid on relay peers, so a peer on both transports sees two creations of one task. Documented as a known limit of the experimental relay in 0.5.4.
nodes.prompt: Carry only events above the relay push cursor and report (or refuse) an adoption whose events the relay already published; or republish under the new uid with a rebind. Red-first with a relay peer and a hub peer.
nodes.acceptance: A peer on both transports sees one task after an adoption; tests; the relay docs' limit removed.

nodes.title: First pull after upgrade: a 0.5.3 unclaim-then-claim reassignment can be hidden by a teammate's later unclaim of the shared claim
nodes.description: Residual of MTIX-95.31.15 (run MTIX-95.31.15.1-4). The first automatic import after upgrading lets a teammate's unclaim explain (apply over) the local assignee only when the local latest claim entry's author equals the local assignee. A local copy on 0.5.3 that unclaimed the shared claim and was then claimed by a different agent, without pushing, passes that check; if the teammate later unclaims the shared claim, the import silently clears the new local claim. Cause: no per-node record of the last exchanged board exists; the conflict baseline (.mtix/data/sync-db.sha256, MTIX-95.31.11) is only a whole-store hash, and boards from 0.5.3 or older carry no activity.

Stores upgraded from 0.5.3 have no snapshot: keep the claim-entry-author check there and document it. Also consider using it for every field explanation. Red-first with real binaries (v0.5.3-beta): A unclaims and a different agent claims on 0.5.3, unpushed; B (0.5.4+) unclaims the shared claim; A upgrades and pulls → refused with the loss list.
nodes.acceptance: Red-first sqlite, service and real-binary tests; with a snapshot present the case is refused and the shared-claim unclaim still applies; snapshot writes atomic and covered; docs (USERMANUAL, TROUBLESHOOTING + template, admin skill + mirrors, EXPORT-FORMAT, CHANGELOG) updated; the MTIX-95.31.15 limits sentence updated.

Without such a record no import can tell an unpushed local change from a teammate's change. Recording it from 0.5.4 on lets the 0.6.0 import be exact for every store that ran 0.5.4.

Then implement the writer only (no import behaviour change in 0.5.4), with red-first tests: written on import/export, unchanged by a local mutation, atomic under a crash (temp file never read), concurrent with the shared lock. Doctor shows whether the record exists. Docs: EXPORT-FORMAT.md and USERMANUAL storage section; no agent-facing behaviour change.

nodes.title: Every task change is logged on the task with a timestamp: field, old value, new value, actor and origin
nodes.description: Maintainer request (2026-10-02), to aid conflict resolution. Today the task's activity log misses several writes (mtix update --assignee, automatic blocking/unblocking from dependencies, changes applied from the hub), and boards from 0.5.3 or older carry no activity, so a merge cannot show who changed a field or when (MTIX-95.31.13 analysis, MTIX-95.31.15). A complete, timestamped per-task change log gives the conflict list real evidence and, with the exchange record (MTIX-95.31.18) and git's merge-base board, enables an automatic three-way merge in 0.6.0. Timestamps from different machines can skew, so the log is evidence (shown to the human/agent, one input to a 3-way merge), never a standalone last-writer judge.
nodes.prompt: Design note first: entry shape (field, old, new, actor, origin: local|import|hub|system, timestamp from the injected clock, causal reference such as the event id/vector clock), which writes append (every field write in the service and store layers; grep for every UPDATE nodes SET), how it is exported/imported in the board (schema version bump, back-compat with 1.0.0/2.0.0 readers), size bounds and compaction, and privacy (no content dumps of large fields: store a hash for prompt/description). Then implement red-first: a table over every write path proving an entry is appended; export/import round trip; merge keeps both sides' entries (union by id); mtix show --history renders it; the MTIX-95.31.13 conflict list shows each side's entries for the conflicting field.

nodes.title: Land the reviewed MTIX-95.31.2 auto-import guard with its round-3 review fixes (merge renumbers a same-id local task)
nodes.description: The HyperSWE loop closed the MTIX-95.31.2 run (auto-import switch and safety net: the P1 data-loss bug the HyperSWE team reported) as failed after its third RED round. Round 3 met every story. One S1 remained: when the store and a pulled .mtix/tasks.json hold DIFFERENT tasks under the same id (different non-empty uids), the refusal describes the difference as field or activity loss. The command it recommends, `mtix import .mtix/tasks.json --mode merge`, then overwrites the local task (title, description, uid), and no backup holds it. This ticket lands the reviewed round-3 code plus the fixes decided from the round-3 review, in a fresh loop run on release/0.5.x. Scope: exactly MTIX-95.31.2's scope plus the items below. The other round-3 findings are separate follow-ups.
nodes.prompt:
1. Recovered base. In the loop worktree (release/0.5.x at 3c7d835), apply internal-docs/orchestration/recovered/MTIX-95.31.2-round3-final.patch from the main checkout (sha256 7248c16b4ad65367b4516832bdf8a27d0a0bb949195aa3008924eb99b3131ff3). If the file is missing, regenerate it with `mgit export --task-id MTIX-95.31.2 --format git` run in ../mtix-release. The patch must apply cleanly and build. This is the reviewed round-3 state: change it only as the items below require. The round-3 review and its decisions are in the same folder (MTIX-95.31.2-round3-review.txt, MTIX-95.31.2-round3-decisions.txt).
2. S1, a different task under the same id (internal/store/sqlite/import_replace_diff.go DiffReplace; internal/store/sqlite/import_uid.go Store.ImportReconcile; internal/service/sync_autoimport_guard.go refusal text):
   a. DiffReplace reports a node whose id holds different non-empty uids locally and in the file as a whole-task loss, worded "a different task under this id" and naming both titles. It counts as lossy.
   b. Merge (mtix import --mode merge, ImportReconcile) never overwrites that local task. It renumbers the LOCAL task and its subtree to the next number that is free in BOTH the store and the incoming file under the same parent. The task keeps its uid. Use the existing renumber path (Store.RenumberSubtree / lockNodeForRenumber), refactored to run inside the import transaction. Bump the sequence counter so later creates do not reuse the number. Then import the file's task at the id: the published board keeps the number. The renumber mutates a non-empty live store, so per ADR-003 section 6 it is reported (the remap: uid, old id, new id; --remap-file writes it) and applied only with --confirm. Without --confirm, nothing is written and the report says to rerun with --confirm.
   c. The refusal's resolution text says exactly this, as do FR-15.2i in REQUIREMENTS.md, USERMANUAL (~1318), the admin skill template and its .claude-plugin mirror, and CHANGELOG, and every other place that says merge keeps local tasks.
   d. Red-first tests (against the recovered round-3 state):
      - Two stores each create PROJ-3 independently, and store A pulls B's board. The auto-import refuses, naming "a different task under this id". Merge without --confirm writes nothing. Merge with --confirm leaves B's task at PROJ-3 and A's task at the next free number, with its uid, title, description, annotations and activity intact. A's export then imports cleanly into B.
      - A task created while a refusal is pending, which reuses a pulled id, is renumbered by the merge, not lost.
3. S2 (internal/service/sync_service.go, around line 199): when a conflict is recorded for a file whose replace would also lose data, keep and print the loss list (or keep the lossy record while that file is pending). The conflict's replace option names what a replace would delete. Red-first test: a lossy refusal, then a local write, then the next command still reports the loss list.
4. S2 (internal/service/sync_service.go, around line 114; internal/store/sqlite/import.go Store.Import): inside its own transaction, the replace re-checks that the store is unchanged since the loss check. Use the same export hash, or a fingerprint that changes on every write (node count, max updated_at, annotation, activity and dependency counts, deleted state). If the store changed, write nothing (the nothingWritten path), so the next command runs the guard again. Red-first deterministic test: fire a write between the diff and the replace (through an injected seam or a hook on the sync_import_triggered log), then assert that the write survives and nothing was imported.
5. Docs:
   - The fail-open direction goes in FR-15.2i, the admin skill and its mirror, USERMANUAL and CHANGELOG: a teammate copy with a later updated_at that missed a local update or delete (neither records activity) is applied as current.
   - claude.md.tmpl and agents.md.tmpl (and docs/AGENTS.md and any generated mirror) tell agents to run `mtix sync` before committing or pushing .mtix/tasks.json. MCP tool results do not show the pending notice.
   - USERMANUAL (~1287) and FR-15.2c say that a write's export, including `mtix import` of another file, imports a changed board first.
6. Tests for two surviving mutations:
   (a) A store with nodes, no sync.sha256, auto_sync false and a changed board, then a write: the board is kept and a pending not_imported refusal is recorded (sync_export_guard.go around line 99).
   (b) In TestAutoExport_BoardChangedOnDisk_NeverOverwritten case 1, assert that LastRefusal is nil after a successful import (sync_export_guard.go around line 69).
7. Out of scope, filed separately:
   - causal descent (activity entries for update and delete);
   - an MCP warning for pending refusals;
   - init adding .mtix/data/ to .gitignore;
   - seeding sequences from a pending board.
Constraints: the mtix-dev directives; red-first for items 2, 3, 4 and 6; provider-neutral docs; no customer data. CHANGELOG: amend the recovered MTIX-95.31.2 bullet and add no second bullet for it.
nodes.acceptance:
- The change equals the recovered MTIX-95.31.2 round-3 diff plus only what the items below require.
- A same-id, different-uid node is refused as "a different task under this id". Merge renumbers the local task to the next free number (in the store and the file), keeps its uid, reports the remap and applies only with --confirm. The two-clone and create-while-pending tests pass (red-first).
- A conflict keeps and prints the loss list, and its replace option names what would be deleted (red-first).
- The replace writes nothing when the store changed after the loss check, and the concurrent write survives (red-first, deterministic).
- Docs: the merge wording, the fail-open direction, the `mtix sync` step before committing the board (agent templates and mirrors) and the FR-15.2c amendment are all in place (REQUIREMENTS, USERMANUAL, admin skill and mirror, claude.md.tmpl, agents.md.tmpl, docs/AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG).
- The tests for the missing sync.sha256 and for no refusal after a successful import pass.
- All six MTIX-95.31.2 stories still hold, and the bar passes: golangci-lint and make test-race.

nodes.title: Sync renumber path applies a renumbered creation's later events under the old number, corrupting a teammate's task
nodes.description:
Reproduced by the MTIX-95.12 round-2 reviewer with built binaries, on the change AND on base release dcc9a62 (a plain offline create, prefix OFFB). It is not caused by 95.12.
The scenario:
1. Replica A creates PROJ-1.1 offline, then claims it and creates a child PROJ-1.1.1. All of it is pending.
2. Replica B creates its own PROJ-1.1 and pushes first.
3. A pushes. The hub reports a renumber collision for A's create_node ("1 renumbered"), but ACCEPTS A's later events in the same batch (the claim and the child create) under the OLD number PROJ-1.1.
4. B's pull applies A's claim to B's PROJ-1.1 (in_progress, assignee agent-a), and a phantom PROJ-1.1.1 appears under B's task.
5. A's own copies become PROJ-1.2 and PROJ-1.2.1.
6. A fresh clone of that hub then fails ("node CLK-1.1 (uid=""): not found").
7. A's pull also applies B's edits of B's PROJ-1.1 to A's pending same-numbered task.
Result: silent cross-task corruption on every replica. 0.5.x events carry no uid, so events apply by node_id.
nodes.acceptance: In the two-replica collision, B's task is never touched by A's events, A's work lands entirely under its new number on every replica, and a fresh clone succeeds. Tests on a throwaway hub. Docs (USERMANUAL sync collisions, admin skill, SYNC-PROTOCOL) describe the behaviour.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: A pulled or cloned task does not advance the local ID counter, so the next create collides
nodes.description:
Found by the MTIX-95.12 round-3 reviewer, end to end with built binaries on a throwaway hub: on a store fresh from `mtix sync clone`, the first `mtix create` fails with "node TEST-1 already exists"; a retry succeeds. Pre-existing, not caused by 95.12.

Likely cause (verified by reading, not yet by a test): import rebuilds the sequences table from node data (internal/store/sqlite/import.go rebuildSequences, FR-7.8.x), but applying a pulled create_node event (internal/store/sqlite/sync_apply.go, case model.OpCreateNode) never advances the sequence counter for the node's parent key. So after a clone, and probably after any pull that brings a teammate's new tasks, the local counter is behind the highest existing sequence, and the next local create picks a taken number. How many retries a user needs after k pulled creates is not yet measured.
nodes.prompt:
1. Reproduce red-first in a test: apply a pulled create_node for PROJ-3 (and a child PROJ-3.2) to a store whose sequences are behind, then create locally under the same parent: today the create fails with ErrAlreadyExists. Also cover the clone path (sync clone into an empty store, then mtix create) and a normal pull of a teammate's new tasks.
2. Fix in the apply path: when a create_node is applied, advance the sequence counter for its parent key to at least the node's seq, in the same transaction (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET value = max(value, excluded.value)). Parameterized SQL only. Do the same for any renumber path that inserts nodes and skips it.
3. Measure and record in the ticket how many failed creates the bug causes today after k pulled creates, and whether a failed create advances the counter (the retry succeeded in the reproduction).
4. Doctor: if a store's sequence counters are behind existing nodes, report it and name the fix (mtix verify or an import rebuild), unless such a check already exists.
nodes.acceptance:
- A test proves the failure on the current code and passes after the fix: after a clone, and after a pull of k teammate creates, the next local create succeeds at the first attempt with the next free number.
- Applying a create_node advances the counter in the same transaction; an idempotent re-apply does not change it.
- CHANGELOG Fixed entry; agent docs updated only if agent-visible behaviour changes.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Push fails spuriously at the reread bound when many events are held and another writer is active
nodes.description:
Follow-up from the MTIX-95.12 final independent review (S3; the run was GREEN at its last round, and this finding is filed by hand because the run cannot be approved, see HyperSWE report 33). It applies to the MTIX-95.12 code (cmd/mtix/sync_push_hold_release.go, around the 16-read bound).

With many held push events, each reread reads every held event (HeldPushEvents(-1), payloads included), rebuilds the index and decides the batch again. The window that a concurrent commit has to miss therefore grows with the held backlog.

Probe (fake hub; a second connection inserts an unrelated row at a fixed interval while 500 edits push):
- 10001 held: every push fails at about 32 commits/s and passes at about 19/s.
- 3001 held: fails at about 170/s.
- 501 held: fails at about 350/s.
- 1 held: fails only against about 6000/s.

The push stops at batch 1 with "the store kept changing while push read its held creations; push again", and it keeps failing while the writer runs (for example a pull applying a backlog, or several agents). Nothing wrong is sent and nothing is lost, and the pre-push hook still continues. But the base never failed for this reason, and no user doc names the error or its recovery.
nodes.prompt:
In cmd/mtix/sync_push_hold_release.go (the held-index reread loop, bounded at 16 reads), stop failing after the last reread. Make the final attempt read the held creations and the batch's tasks and record the holds under the write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), or read both in one read transaction.

Reread only the held create_node rows, without payloads.

Red-first with the reviewer's probe shape: a fake hub, a concurrent writer at a fixed interval, and 501 and 3001 held events. Push must complete.

Name the error and "push again" in the USERMANUAL troubleshooting section, and in the admin skill with its plugin mirrors if the error remains possible.
nodes.acceptance:
- With 3001 held events and a concurrent writer at 100+ commits/s, push completes (red-first against the MTIX-95.12 code).
- No held event is sent, and no event is lost.
- Rereads read only held create_node rows, without payloads.
- Docs name any remaining error and its recovery.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Pull pagination must not skip events that share a Lamport value across a page boundary; clone sets the pull cursor
nodes.description: The pull and clone cursor is the batch's maximum Lamport value, and the next query is `lamport_clock > $1 ORDER BY lamport_clock LIMIT n` with no tiebreak. Events that share that Lamport value but did not fit on the page are never pulled. Separately, clone never writes the pull cursor, even though its doc comment says it does, so the first pull after a clone re-reads the whole hub. The batch apply and the cursor write also happen in separate local transactions. ADR-006 D6, D16.
nodes.prompt:
Files: internal/store/postgres/transport/push_pull.go (PullEvents), cmd/mtix/sync_pull.go, cmd/mtix/sync_clone.go, internal/store/sqlite/schema.go (meta seed).
Keyset on the tuple: `WHERE (lamport_clock, event_id) > ($1, $2) ORDER BY lamport_clock, event_id LIMIT $3`. Add meta.sync.last_pulled_event_id, default ''. The empty string sorts first, so an upgraded client re-reads events at exactly last_pulled_clock, which is idempotent. Apply the same keyset to the clone checkpoint. Clone writes both cursor keys on completion. Write the cursor in the same local transaction as the batch apply.
Performance: an index on (lamport_clock, event_id) is an additive, idempotent migration (`CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`). Migrations only run on `sync init`; the query is correct without the index, just slower. Document this.
nodes.acceptance:
Red-first:
1. TestPullEvents_EqualLamportAcrossPageBoundary_NoneSkipped: real Postgres, limit 2, three events with the same Lamport.
2. TestClone_SetsPullCursor: the first pull after a clone fetches only newer events.
3. TestPullLoop_CursorWrittenWithBatchApply: a crash between apply and cursor write is impossible by construction.
4. An upgrade from an old cursor re-reads the boundary Lamport idempotently (test).
5. Migration adds the index idempotently.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Backport MTIX-91 to 0.5.4: sync push sends each event's uid
nodes.description:
Maintainer decision 2026-09-26: backport MTIX-91 to 0.5.4.

On release/0.5.x, sync push never sends an event's uid (the pending read omits the column), so the hub stores uid NULL and treats a re-emitted create as a different node. The ADR-003 same-node no-op can never fire, and the hub asks for renumbers instead. The MTIX-95.12 run-2 reviewer observed pushed events reaching the hub "with no uid".

The fix is on main as 6d2af9f (MTIX-91: carry uid on the pending read). Merge-forward #8 (release → main) then combined it with MTIX-95.12's push-hold reads into one store projection: ReadPendingEventsAfter, ReadPendingEventsByID and a shared scanner, all carrying uid. The same code must now land on release, so both lines share it and later merge-forwards stay clean.
nodes.prompt:
On release/0.5.x, through the review loop (fix only):
1. Port the store projection from main's merge-forward #8 commit (internal/store/sqlite/sync_pending.go: ReadPendingEvents, ReadPendingEventsAfter, ReadPendingEventsByID and the scanner, all selecting uid) and the CLI delegation in cmd/mtix/sync_push.go and sync_push_hold_release.go, so push sends uid on the pending read AND the held-event re-read.
2. Port MTIX-91's and merge-forward #8's tests: the store uid tests, and the CLI wire test cmd/mtix/sync_push_wire_uid_test.go. Show them red first on release.
3. Name the source commits in the ticket and in every commit body: 6d2af9f and the merge-forward #8 merge commit.
4. The e2e harness shares the same projection.
5. Add a CHANGELOG Fixed entry (0.5.4). Update the agent docs if anything visible to agents changes.
6. Also remove the duplicated MTIX-95.31.2 CHANGELOG bullet (MTIX-95.42), as its own story.
Run PG16/PG17 hub tests (throwaway containers via the orchestration tools): an old create re-pushed after the fix is a same-node no-op for rows pushed WITH uid.
nodes.acceptance:
- Push sends each event's uid on both push paths (red-first on release; wire test through the fake hub).
- A re-pushed create whose hub row carries the uid is a same-node no-op on PG16 and PG17.
- The code equals main's projection, so the next merge-forward has no conflict in these files.
- The CHANGELOG entry is added; provenance is recorded.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: sync migrate --yes can leave the node-number registry index INVALID, so the registry is silently not enforced
nodes.description: Found by the MTIX-95.1.8 developer (2026-09-26), verified on PG16 with a throwaway hub; pre-existing. The dedup sweep is append-only and leaves the duplicate create rows in place. So when the version gate is open, the owner's 'mtix sync migrate --yes' fails with a unique violation (SQLSTATE 23505) while building sync_events_node_registry_uidx CONCURRENTLY. A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID, not-ready index behind. After that, '--yes' reports 'registry index already present', and init's CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS skips it, so the node-number registry is not enforced and nothing reports it.

3. Red-first on PG16 and PG17 with the developer's scenario, using throwaway containers via the orchestration tools.
4. Doctor check plus agent docs (Commandment 15).

- migrate --yes on a hub with duplicates ends with a VALID registry index, or refuses with an exact, actionable message; it never leaves an INVALID index reported as present.

nodes.title: Lookups by task uid scan every node: the partial uid index is never used
nodes.description: Found while preparing the 0.5.4 batch (release b597bb0). idx_nodes_uid is a partial index: ON nodes(uid) WHERE uid IS NOT NULL AND uid <> '' (internal/store/sqlite/schema.go:104). SQLite uses a partial index only when the query's WHERE implies the index's WHERE; 'uid = ?' with a bound value implies 'uid IS NOT NULL' but not "uid <> ''", so every lookup by uid is a full scan of nodes (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: SCAN nodes). Affected: internal/store/sqlite/sync_apply.go:965 (resolveNodeRef, per pulled event carrying a uid), settle.go:297, node_uid.go:40, import_local_renumber.go:447; sync_repair_status_rules.go:116 already adds the term (on sync_events). Today pulled events rarely carry a uid, but MTIX-95.41 (MTIX-91 backport) makes push send uids, so after 0.5.4 every pulled event with a uid scans every node: O(nodes × events) on large stores. Main has the same queries (MTIX-91 is there).
nodes.prompt: On release/0.5.x through the review loop: add "AND uid <> ''" to every nodes lookup by uid (the four sites above, and any other found by grep), so idx_nodes_uid is usable; the empty uid is never looked up by these paths (callers guard e.UID != ""), so behaviour is unchanged. Red-first: a table-driven test runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for each lookup query on a real store and asserts it uses idx_nodes_uid (fails today with SCAN nodes). Add a guard test so a new 'nodes WHERE uid = ?' query without the term fails (e.g. scan the sqlite package's SQL strings, or assert the plan for a shared helper). No schema change. CHANGELOG Fixed entry (performance). Merge forward to main.

nodes.title: Pull must also fetch late-arriving events stamped below the cursor (containment for Lamport-cursor gaps)
nodes.description: The hub stores the Lamport value each client stamps, and pull asks for lamport_clock > cursor. A writer that was offline pushes events stamped lower than busier peers' cursors, so those peers never pull them and replicas silently diverge. The complete fix is a hub-assigned, commit-ordered sequence (ADR-006 phase 2, protocol 2). This child is the 0.5.x containment, with no schema change. ADR-006 D5, S6.
nodes.prompt:
Files: cmd/mtix/sync_pull.go, transport (new query), internal/store/sqlite (meta key).
After the normal cursor loop, sweep: `SELECT event_id, now() FROM sync_events WHERE created_at >= $1`, where $1 = the previous sweep's hub time minus a 15-minute overlap. Use hub time only, never the client clock. Diff the ids against local sync_events, fetch the missing rows by id, and apply them through the normal ingest path.
Recovered events are by definition late and low-Lamport. Workflow events among them must go through the winner rule from MTIX-95.10, otherwise every recovered claim reverts newer status (review F-43; internal-docs/reviews/ADR-006-FR-23-review-2026-09-23.md). This child therefore depends on 95.10.
Store meta.sync.last_sweep_at (hub time). The first sweep after upgrade diffs the full id history once, paged, and prints 'N late events recovered'. created_at is the hub transaction start time, so the overlap must exceed the longest push transaction (statement_timeout 10s); 15 minutes is ample.
Performance: ship an index on created_at as an additive, idempotent migration, created only when absent, or state the per-pull scan cost measured at 100K and 1M events.
`mtix sync status` shows the last sweep time.
nodes.acceptance:
Red-first on real Postgres:

nodes.title: mtix sync repair --status: re-derive workflow state from the event log to heal replay reverts
nodes.description: Installations that pulled while holding unpushed, newer status changes may have nodes whose status, assignee, agent_state or closed_at were reverted by a replayed older event. Leaf progress can also be wrong on replicas that applied a done transition, because apply never sets it. Provide a safe, auditable repair that derives the intended state from the local event log. Depends on .2: without it, the next pull re-reverts.
nodes.prompt:
Service-layer method plus a thin CLI: `mtix sync repair --status` (dry-run by default) and `--apply`.
For each live node, collect its local sync_events that write workflow state: transition_status, claim, unclaim, defer, and update_field for status/assignee/agent_state. Pick the winner by (lamport_clock DESC, wall_clock_ts DESC, author_machine_hash ASC, event_id DESC). Compute the expected status, assignee, agent_state, closed_at and defer_until, plus leaf progress (1.0 if done, else unchanged), and compare with the row.
Dry-run prints a table of differences, with --json available.
--apply: first take a verified snapshot, .mtix/data/backups/pre-repair-status-<time>.db, using the MTIX-90 snapshot machinery. Then apply each correction through a repair-specific store path in one transaction per node. That path emits a transition_status event (from = current, to = expected, reason 'sync repair'), so other replicas converge. It writes activity/audit entries and recomputes parent progress and dependents in the same transaction, as the normal transition does. It validates against the event-derived target instead of the interactive state machine, and records why.
nodes.acceptance:
1. TestSyncRepairStatus_DryRun_ListsReplayRevert: the S7 fixture shows one difference.

4. Nodes without workflow events are untouched; leaf progress is fixed for done nodes.
5. Reachable via the service layer only (no store access from cmd).

nodes.title: Sync redesign phase 1: FR-18 audit, independent design review, accepted design, requirements, verification harness
nodes.description: ADR-006 (the sync replication core) and FR-23 (the read-only hub viewer) are proposed designs. Before any redesign code is written, phase 1 establishes three things. First, the true conformance of today's sync against FR-18 and its design documents: the previous audit signed off requirements that do not hold. Second, an independent, adversarial review of both designs and a decision on every open question. Third, the requirements and the verification harness that every later phase is measured against: the projector property framework, a deterministic multi-replica simulator, and one transport contract suite shared by the fake hub and real Postgres. Every known defect becomes an expected-failure test that alerts the moment it is fixed.

Originating ask (maintainer, 2026-09-23): 'do we need to do an audit first of our FR?'; then 'give me a prompt for the audit agent to validate the ADR-006 and FR-23 independent design review' and 'Proceed to create Phase 1 epic'. The agreed answer: no audit gate before the phase-0 containment, but a stricter FR-18 audit and an independent design review before redesign code. Order: .1 and .2 in parallel; .3 decisions after both; then .4 requirements and .5-.7 harness; then .8 expected-failure catalog.

Common rules for every child of this epic:
- Read the dev directives (CLAUDE.md, imported from ../mtix-dev/CLAUDE.md) first. TDD red-first.
- Phase 1 work lands on main (branch feat|test|docs/MTIX-<id>/<desc> off main). It runs in parallel with the phase-0 containment epic MTIX-95 on release/0.5.x. Do not modify phase-0 code paths except through merges.
- Maintainer design records (gitignored, local only): internal-docs/ADR-006-SYNC-REPLICATION-CORE.md, internal-docs/FR-23-HUB-VIEWER.md. Security-sensitive findings stay in internal-docs until their fix ships.
- Never put customer data or provider recommendations in code, tests, comments, commits, tickets or public docs (tasks.json is a public export).

1. FR-18 conformance audit report delivered, with verified-red evidence per requirement (.1).
2. Independent review report delivered; every finding dispositioned (.2, .3).
3. ADR-006 and FR-23 status Accepted; every open decision recorded with rationale (.3).
4. FR-18 amendments merged into REQUIREMENTS.md, with traceability entries (.4).
5. Harness merged and green in CI: projector property framework, multi-replica simulator, transport contract suite (.5-.7).

nodes.title: FR-18 conformance audit with verified-red evidence (spec vs code vs tests)
nodes.description: The phase-1 investigation found many normative statements that the code does not meet. Examples: an audit mechanism that is specified but not implemented; convergence tests that shuffle only causally-ordered update and comment events; protocol versioning that was never built; backup coverage; conflict resolution that never writes the superseding event its design describes. The previous audit (docs/audit/MTIX-15-audit-pass2.md) signed off such items by citing test names. This audit establishes the true state with a stricter method.
nodes.prompt:
Scope: every MUST/SHALL in REQUIREMENTS.md FR-18.1-18.28, every normative statement in docs/SYNC-DESIGN.md, docs/SYNC-PROTOCOL.md and docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md (including every threat mitigation T1-T20), and every evidence row of docs/audit/MTIX-15-audit-pass2.md.
Method, verified-red: for each item, locate the enforcing code (file:line) and the test that proves it. Then demonstrate that the test fails under a targeted mutation of the enforcing code, in a throwaway git worktree outside the repo (git worktree add <tmp> main; mutate; run the single test; remove the worktree). An item is MET only with that red evidence. Otherwise it is UNTESTED, PARTIAL or NOT MET, with the gap stated.
Also record items that are documented but have no code at all (Commandment 11), and code behaviour that no document describes.
Read-only on the repo: no tracked-file edits, no mtix writes. Parallel sub-agents by section are fine; consolidate into one report.
Output: internal-docs/audit/FR-18-conformance-<date>.md (internal first; security-relevant rows stay internal). After the phase-0 release, publish a sanitized version to docs/audit/. Feed the gaps into .4 and .8.
nodes.acceptance:
1. Report lists every FR-18.x and design/threat-model claim with a status of MET, PARTIAL, UNTESTED or NOT MET, and evidence: file:line, the test name, and the mutation that turned it red (for MET).

nodes.title: Design: large content and attachments (screenshots, videos) for sync protocol 2
nodes.description:
Maintainer decision 2026-09-25 on MTIX-95.12 (internal-docs/orchestration/decision-95.12-field-limits.md): v0.5.4 ships option A (hold and report). For 0.6.0 the maintainer rejected designing around the 64 KiB event cap: tickets will carry screenshots and bug-reproduction videos, so shrinking local limits to fit the cap (option B as written) or splitting text across events is not acceptable on its own. A proper design is required. This resolves the open item in ADR-006 section 12: "v2 handling of fields larger than the 64 KiB wire cap: align local limits, or split fields across events (F-15)".

Why the cap exists today (FR-18.7, SYNC-DESIGN 5.1, internal/sync/validator/validator.go MaxPayloadBytes): it bounds memory per request (push batch 100 events, pull page 1000 events), bounds hub growth under keep-forever retention (every clone downloads the whole log), and limits damage from a buggy or hostile client or hub. The number 64 KiB has no written rationale. It contradicts the local limits (prompt 100 KB, description 50 KB, later edits unchecked) and JSON escaping can grow text six-fold. The FR-21 relay frames records at 128 KiB.
nodes.prompt:
Produce a design (a new FR, or an ADR-006 section, whichever the maintainer prefers) for large content in sync protocol 2, then take it through an independent adversarial design review and a maintainer decision. Nothing is built under this ticket.

The design must answer, with trade-offs and a recommendation for each:
1. Model: separate large content from events. Events stay small and bounded; they carry a reference (content hash such as SHA-256, size, media type, name). Large text fields above a threshold and binary attachments (images, video, logs, archives) travel as content-addressed blobs. Define the threshold, or justify raising the event cap to fit local limits including JSON growth.
2. Hub storage without new infrastructure: blobs must work on plain PostgreSQL (for example a chunked side table), with an optional external object store described only by capability (provider-neutral). Scale-to-zero: no timers, no background work; fetch on demand.
3. Transport: chunked, resumable, integrity-checked upload and download; dedupe by hash; per-blob and per-project quotas configurable in MB/GB; memory stays bounded because blobs are streamed, never buffered whole.
4. Clone and pull cost: metadata eager, blob bodies lazy; local cache with eviction; what an offline replica sees for a blob it has not fetched.
5. The FR-21 file relay: whether and how it carries blobs (record cap 128 KiB means chunking) or explicitly refuses them.
6. Erasure and privacy: screenshots and videos can hold personal data. Blobs must be erasable outside the write-once log, consistent with ADR-006 decision 4 (redactable payloads, owner-only redact).
7. Security: size and type validation at every boundary, no execution, safe rendering in the web UI and the hub viewer (FR-23), including SVG and HTML; content-type sniffing rules.
8. Local store: SQLite size, backup and restore size, recover, and tasks.json export (never inline blob bodies).
9. Agent use: CLI and MCP commands to attach, list, fetch and remove; how mtix context and prompt assembly reference attachments for multimodal agents; doctor checks.
10. Compatibility: 0.5.x clients and hubs never receive blobs; behaviour at the protocol-2 cutover.
Record the answers in ADR-006 section 12 (replacing the F-15 open item) and in REQUIREMENTS.md once accepted.
nodes.acceptance:
- A design document answers items 1-10 with a recommendation each, provider-neutral, and states hub cost and scale-to-zero behaviour.
- An independent adversarial design review (a session that did not write the design) has been run and its findings dispositioned.
- The maintainer has accepted the design; ADR-006 section 12 no longer lists the 64 KiB item as open; follow-up build tickets are filed with full description, prompt and acceptance.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Registry index above the left-out cap: a registry table maintained by the hub for hubs with many historical duplicate creates
nodes.description: From the MTIX-95.44 design (internal-docs/orchestration/design-MTIX-95.44.md §6): in 0.5.4 the unique node-number registry index names its left-out historical duplicate creates in its predicate, which must fit one pg_index row, so migrate refuses above a measured cap. A hub above the cap keeps working without the index. A durable design (e.g. a registry table maintained by a trigger, or the protocol-2 registry in ADR-006) removes the cap.
nodes.prompt: Design and implement a registry that enforces one create per (project, node number) without a size-limited predicate, compatible with append-only sync_events and backup/restore (functions are not in the dump). Covers migration from the 0.5.4 predicate index.
nodes.acceptance: - No cap on historical duplicates. - Backup/restore round-trips. - Migration from the 0.5.4 index. - PG16/PG17 tests.

nodes.title: Independent adversarial design review of ADR-006 and FR-23
nodes.description: ADR-006 and FR-23 were written by the same investigation that found the defects. Before they are accepted, an independent reviewer who did not write them must try to break them: verify the defect census and the technical claims by experiment, attempt a counterexample for every invariant, check directive compliance, and recommend a decision for every open question.
nodes.prompt:
Run the review exactly as specified in the self-contained reviewer prompt internal-docs/reviews/ADR-006-FR-23-design-review-prompt.md. Hand that file, unchanged, to a fresh agent session that did not author the documents; parallel sub-reviewers by area are encouraged.
The reviewer is read-only on the repo (temporary experiments deleted), uses no live systems (a local disposable Postgres only), and writes one report: internal-docs/reviews/ADR-006-FR-23-review-<date>.md.
The maintainer reads the report. Findings and open-decision recommendations are dispositioned in .3, not here.
nodes.acceptance:
1. The report exists with: a verdict per document; a findings table with severity and CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/REFUTED; a counterexample log for I1-I12; OD recommendations; required changes as proposed edits; the list of experiments run.
2. The review was performed by a session that did not author ADR-006/FR-23, which the report states.
3. No tracked file changed.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Resolve open decisions and finalize ADR-006 and FR-23 (Proposed -> Accepted)
nodes.description: Both documents carry open decisions: cutover strategy, cancel-cascade semantics, undelete, version-vector keying, claim arbitration, CLI naming, retention, the viewer's auth and templates, and more. Combine the audit (.1) and the review (.2) into maintainer decisions and accepted documents.
nodes.prompt:
For every review finding, record a disposition: accepted (with the document edit), rejected (with rationale), or deferred (with the phase). For every OD in ADR-006 section 12 and FR-23 section 15, record the maintainer's decision and rationale in a decision log appended to each document. Apply the edits, set Status to Accepted with the date, and bump the document versions.
Decisions are the maintainer's: prepare a one-page decision brief per OD (options, the reviewer's recommendation, consequences) and ask. Do not decide on the maintainer's behalf.
Split any accepted change that alters phase-0 scope into MTIX-95 follow-ups.

nodes.title: Projector property-test framework: arbitrary order, duplicates, all op types
nodes.description: Today's convergence property tests shuffle only causally-ordered sequences of update and comment events and never duplicate an event. The redesign's first invariant requires identical state for any delivery order and any duplication, across every op type. Build the framework before the projector, and run it against today's apply engine to record the failures as expected.
nodes.prompt:
New package internal/sync/projecttest, test-only helpers:
- Seeded generators for every op type: create, update_field (every whitelisted field), set_prompt, set_acceptance, transition, claim, unclaim, defer, comment, link/unlink dep, delete, and undelete once it exists. Generators produce concurrent histories across several authors and replicas, respecting only emission order within a replica.
- An Oracle interface, Apply(events) -> digest, with adapters for today's IdempotentApply engine (SQLite) and, later, the pure projector.
- A canonical state digest over synced columns, excluding declared local-only columns (the list comes from the accepted ADR-006).
- Properties: permutation invariance (arbitrary, not only causal), duplicate idempotence, incremental equals batch, conflict-set determinism.
Seeds are controllable via MTIX_PROPERTY_TEST_SEEDS, and a failing seed prints a minimal reproduction. Properties that fail on today's engine are registered as expected failures through .8's registry.
nodes.acceptance:
1. Generators cover every op type (a coverage test asserts it).
2. Against a deliberately order-dependent fake oracle, the permutation and duplicate properties fail: the framework can go red.
3. Against today's engine, the failing properties are recorded as expected failures, not skipped silently.
4. Deterministic by seed, and runs under -race.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Deterministic multi-replica sync simulator (fake hub and relay, seeded scheduler, crash injection)
nodes.description: No existing test runs more than one replica through a hub over time. Every cross-replica defect found in phase 0 (replay, push wedge, cursor gaps) needed a hand-written scenario. Build a deterministic simulator in the style of FoundationDB's simulation testing, so these bugs are found by search instead.
nodes.prompt:
Test-only package internal/sync/simtest. N replicas (real SQLite stores via the service layer), a fake hub, and a fake relay. The fake hub must pass the same contract suite as real Postgres (.7). A seeded scheduler interleaves local mutations, push, pull, relay ticks, offline windows, duplicated or dropped responses, and crashes at every step boundary (inject between hub commit and ack recording, between apply and cursor write, and mid-batch). It also covers hub restore to an earlier snapshot and a replica rejoining after a long offline period.
The fake hub is pluggable: v1 (today's Lamport cursor) and, later, v2 (hub sequence), so the same scenarios measure both.
Invariants checked at quiescence: identical event sets on all replicas; identical state digests (the .5 digest); no pending events; the hub holds the union; conflict sets are identical.
A failing seed reproduces exactly. There is a short CI profile and a long nightly profile. Failures on today's code register as expected through .8.
nodes.acceptance:
1. With the v1 fake hub, the simulator rediscovers, by search, the phase-0 defect classes: own-event replay revert, push wedge after a lost ack, and a missed late push. The report shows the seeds.
2. Seeds are reproducible.
3. Crash injection exists at every listed boundary.
4. CI and nightly profiles are wired.
5. The fake hub passes the .7 contract suite.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Shared transport contract suite: fake hub and real Postgres must pass the same tests
nodes.description: A test-only mirror of production code has drifted before and hidden a bug (MTIX-91). The fake hub used by the simulator must be proven equivalent to the real hub on every behaviour sync relies on, including concurrency and ordering.
nodes.acceptance:
1. The same suite runs green against the fake and against real Postgres.
2. A deliberately diverging fake (fixture) fails the suite.
3. The concurrency test exists for the v2 sequence (expected-fail until phase 2).
4. It runs in the cloud-contract gate.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Expected-failure regression catalog: every confirmed open defect has a test that alerts when fixed
nodes.description: Committing failing tests breaks CI, and skipping them hides regressions. Introduce an expected-failure registry: known-defect tests run, pass while the defect reproduces, and fail CI the moment the defect disappears, so the fixing change must also remove the registration. Then register every confirmed open defect from ADR-006 section 1 and the .1 audit that phase 0 does not fix.
nodes.prompt:
Test helper internal/testutil/knowndefect. Expect(t, defectID, ticketID, fn) runs fn in an isolated sub-test.
- If fn fails: the test passes and logs the defect.
- If fn passes: t.Fatalf('defect <id> no longer reproduces; remove the registration').
A registry test reads .mtix/tasks.json and fails if any registered ticketID is closed, so a ticket cannot be closed while its defect is still registered as expected. Register the property failures from .5, the simulator seeds from .6, and one focused regression per confirmed defect (for example: apply emits new events; cascade delete not replicated; progress not set on apply; comment id divergence; poison event stalls pull; relay one-way gateway; backup and restore gaps).
Each regression is proven to reproduce on today's code at registration time.
nodes.acceptance:
1. knowndefect helper with unit tests covering both directions (expected fail passes; unexpected pass fails).
2. The registry-to-ticket consistency test exists.
3. Every confirmed open defect not fixed by MTIX-95 is registered with a reproducing test.
4. CI is green, and a simulated fix (fixture) flips its test red.
nodes.creator: cli

nodes.title: Hardening: verification covers role attributes beyond memberships
nodes.description: From the MTIX-95.1.2 round-3 review (sec/0.5.4 223df37): the hub-privileges verification in mtix sync harden and doctor checks privileges and memberships, not role attributes such as REPLICATION. 0.5.4 documents the exclusion (MTIX-95.1.4). This ticket decides whether the check should report such roles.
nodes.prompt: Design and implement reporting of checked roles whose attributes give access to sync-table data outside the privilege system, starting with REPLICATION: report them as information, or as a finding in strict mode. Decide which, and update harden, doctor, the USERMANUAL, the skill and its mirrors, and tests on PG16 and PG17 with throwaway containers. Work on main after the security lane has merged (0.6.0).
nodes.acceptance: A REPLICATION-attribute role that the check covers appears in harden's report (information or a finding, as decided). The docs say how it is treated. There are PG16 and PG17 tests.

nodes.title: mtix show omits annotations, so review verdicts are invisible and a successful annotate looks like a failed write
nodes.description: `mtix show <id>` prints no annotations, although its help says it shows the node's full details and it has no flag to include them. The data exists: `mtix show <id> --json` returns it under .annotations, and `mtix context <id>` renders it. Consequences: (1) a reader using show, the documented view of a node, cannot see annotations; these carry review verdicts, so a node with a FAIL verdict looks as if it has none. (2) `mtix annotate <id>` prints 'Added annotation to <id>', and a following `mtix show <id>` shows no trace of it, so a successful write looks like a failed one.
nodes.prompt:
Files: cmd/mtix/show.go (runShow prints ID, title, status, priority, type, assignee, description, prompt truncated to 100 characters, progress and created; nothing about annotations); internal/mcp/tools_node.go (registerShowTool marshals the whole node, so check whether mtix_show already returns annotations and fix it here only if it has the same gap). Model: internal/model/annotation.go (id, author, text, created_at, resolved, addressee).
Print every annotation after the description, oldest first by created_at (tie-break by id), each with its author and an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Indent multi-line text under its header line. A node with no annotations prints 'Annotations: none', so absence is stated, never silent. --json output is unchanged.
The help text (Short and Long) must describe exactly what the command prints, including that the prompt is truncated and that --json prints the full node record. docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md carries the show help text and must match.
Tests in cmd/mtix (use initTestApp and captureStdout): annotations printed oldest first with author and timestamp; 'Annotations: none'; an annotate-then-show round trip; the help text names every label the command prints; the MCP show tool returns the same annotations, in the same order, as the CLI prints.
Red-first: the new tests fail on current main, pass with the change, and fail again with the change removed. Record all three in the PR body.
CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]. Ticket, commits and PR in product terms only. Do not replace any installed mtix binary; build only to temporary paths.
nodes.acceptance:
1. `mtix show <id>` prints every annotation after the description, oldest first, each with its author and timestamp.
2. A node with no annotations prints 'Annotations: none'.
3. The MCP show tool returns the same annotations the CLI prints.
4. A round-trip test: annotate, then show, and the new annotation appears.
5. The help text describes exactly what the command prints (docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md matches).
6. Red first: the new tests fail on current main, pass with the change, and fail again with the change removed; the PR body shows all three.
7. A CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
8. After merge, report the ticket id, the PR number and the merge commit. Installed binaries are not replaced.

nodes.title: HTTP handlers must go through the service layer (no direct store access)
nodes.description: internal/api/http/server.go holds *sqlite.Store, and handlers call it directly, writes included (for example handlers_workflow.go and handlers_admin.go). This violates Commandment 7 and blocks a compile-time read-only server for FR-23 (review F-67).
nodes.prompt: Inventory every s.store.* call in internal/api/http. Route each through the owning service (node, workflow, admin, dependency); add service methods where missing, with godoc and FR references. The server receives services, not the store. Split read and write capabilities so a read-only server can be built from read interfaces alone (a precursor to FR-23's ReadModel). Do not change HTTP behaviour; existing handler tests must stay green. Note the MCP registry's runtime read-only filter (internal/mcp/registry.go) for a later, similar change.
